\chapter{Frozen proof-report archive:
finite\_volume57}\label{frozen-proof-report-archive-finite_volume57}

This is a mechanical TeX translation of every bound Markdown proof
report, plus prose reports explicitly named by the current proof map. It
accompanies the edited manuscript, exact scripts and partial Lean
development. It is an archival source collection, not a claim of
end-to-end formal verification.

Reports retain their original dates, scopes and historical status
wording. Later reports can supersede earlier bounds. The authoritative
endpoint is
\nolinkurl{results/fresh_d13_context_dimension57_20261018.json}. The
current edited proof map is
\texttt{docs/finite\_volume57\_lemma\_map.md}.

The manifest records all report hashes and every recursively bound file.
This export verifies source identity; it does not reprove the geometry.

compactness, simple-cusp or facet-count hypothesis is required.

\section{Compact arithmetic boundary for an independent
checker}\label{compact-arithmetic-boundary-for-an-independent-checker}

The new finite closure data are in the D13 certificate's \texttt{finite}
object:

\begin{itemize}

  \texttt{all\_old\_costly\_forests}: all eight B13/D13 plus three
  A15/D15 choices, with old378 and new377;
\item
  \texttt{complete\_increasing\_families}: all six D28+two-rank15 or
  A12+D16+two-rank15 forests, with exact old/increment/new costs;
\item
  the exhaustive predecessor count stem and the unchanged ideal
  interface.
\end{itemize}

The source's context delta uses integer units1/64:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{−64 * d13                          if a15+d15 ≥ 3}
\NormalTok{+32 * d28 +64 * a12*d16            if a15+d15 ≥ 2.}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

These inequalities occur only in the rank58 domain; the local theorem
requires distinct whole witness components. The B13 endpoint decrease is
already in the imported \texttt{Z.value}. A checker must prove the
rank-capacity family classification and pointwise complement, not merely
add six numbers. The preceding count's completeness is a separate
internal theorem.

The ideal JSON has2552 rows of rank lists,58 integer coefficients, V,G,
exact rational envelope/margins and the complete normalized envelope
array. An independent checker must enumerate the domain and multiply
each factor polynomial. Symmetry and coefficient sum alone are
insufficient. The final source performs those products directly using
Python integers/Fractions.

The Lean development is tracked in
\href{../formal/README.md}{formal/README.md}. The arithmetic interfaces
are suitable for kernel checks, but complete geometry, every historical
route and the higher tail must also be connected. No end-to-end Lean
verification of57 is asserted by this guide.

\section{Final contradiction}\label{final-contradiction}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{D5 ≤ 377 vf + sum C\_actual}
\NormalTok{D5 ≥ 377 vf + sum kappa + 4205}
\NormalTok{kappa − C\_actual ≥ 36}
\NormalTok{therefore 0 ≥ 4205 + 36 vi \textgreater{} 0.}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The finite equality is sufficient, including vi=0. The global4205 term
is counted once. The completed58 tail handles dimensions≥59. This is the
completed57 theorem, distinct from any future search for56 or
construction of a new finite-volume polytope.

\chapter{General finite-volume bound58: proof and formalization
map}\label{general-finite-volume-bound58-proof-and-formalization-map}

This map concerns \textbf{every finite-sided, finite-volume real
hyperbolic Coxeter polytope}. The completed internal theorem is
\texttt{dimension\ ≤\ 58}. It imposes neither arithmeticity nor
compactness, a simple-cusp condition or a facet bound. The separate
ambient58 research frontier is an attempt to prove57; its current
payment inequalities are not dependencies of the completed58 proof.
Construction and compact-arithmetic experiments are also independent.

The authoritative endpoint is
\href{../results/fresh_a15_d15_dimension58_20261018.md}{the dimension58
composition}. The \href{../manuscripts/finite_volume58.tex}{TeX
manuscript} develops this proof spine.
\href{finite_volume58_reproduce.md}{Reproduction instructions}
distinguish arithmetic replay, source review and formal verification.

\section{Quantified internal lemma
interfaces}\label{quantified-internal-lemma-interfaces}

The following are proof obligations for the internal development. Their
labels are suggested Lean/module names, not declarations of axioms.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{ActualCornerSupport}.} For every actual two-face F of
  a finite-volume Coxeter n-polytope, its n−2 supporting roots W are
  positive definite; adjoining one side gives a positive-definite edge
  principal. At each ideal corner, exactly one irreducible affine factor
  varies, and the other factor pieces are elliptic. This must allow
  nonsimple cusps.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{AffineFactorFiber}.} For any ideal vertex with affine
  factor ranks \texttt{r\ :\ List\ Nat}, all positive and summing to
  n−1, put \texttt{V\ =\ ∏\ (r\_i+1)}. For every marked pair of the i-th
  full affine factor, the number of actual two-face corners representing
  it is exactly \texttt{V/(r\_i+1)}. A connected affine subdiagram used
  in a local proof must first be shown to be the whole actual factor.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{LorentzRadicalSeal}.} Let a norm-two acute core span a
  subspace containing a timelike vector. Every Gram radical is an actual
  zero linear combination of its roots. If all permitted nonzero
  contacts of an additional supporting white must meet two opposite
  radical signs, either the specified retained short path exists or
  every such contact vanishes. The latter conclusion seals all paying
  components, including unmarked witness factors; it is not merely an
  isolated-node test.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{LorentzProjectionExclusion}.} For every allowed
  contact vector q into a nondegenerate Lorentz core G, a prospective
  norm-two root has positive-definite residual square \texttt{2−qᵀG⁻¹q}.
  A projection greater than2 is impossible. Equality forces zero
  residual and exact products with every other core-span root. This
  supplies the saturated-root exclusions.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{CompleteSelectedSupport}.} Every remaining actual
  quadrilateral, after the independent ideal/short-path branches and
  complete low, disjoint, protected and adaptive routes, lies in the
  enumerated native selected domain with its actual marked component
  embedded injectively and inducedly. The order15 domains have536
  patterns each,482 A15 maps and870 D15 maps; failed searches are part
  of completeness. Finite saved corners alone do not establish this
  universal statement.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{LocalPayment59}.} There exists one nonnegative
  intrinsic corner weight rule w such that every triangular two-face has
  total≥2 and every quadrilateral total≥1. Its finite cost is exactly
  the typed rule exported below, and its affine factor costs are bounded
  by c(r). The proof uses \texttt{ActualCornerSupport}, the local
  seals/exclusions and a well-founded priority order. Every later
  replacement must retain the earlier chosen output or supply a new
  independent replacement. It must not be assumed that all short ideal
  paths themselves have unit weight.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{TypedForestDomination59}.} For every finite Coxeter
  forest of rank59, replacing each component by its specified
  representative dominates its base, every pairwise interaction and the
  two guarded context charges. This includes exceptional types and
  arbitrary-label rank-two factors. There are180 actual type
  representatives and32,400 ordered pair checks.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{ForestDomain59}.} Every representative forest
  decomposes into one of961 vectors of fixed ranks9--16 and fixed A17,
  one separately fixed rank5 multiplicity, and residual
  ranks1--4,6--8,17--59. Rank17 residual means D17, not a second copy of
  fixed A17. There are2574 expanded rows. Residual pairwise interactions
  vanish. Their exact items include all interactions with the fixed
  components.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{LastItemUpper}.} For a finite list of positive-rank
  items \texttt{(r,w)} and table V with V(0)=0, if
  \texttt{V(n)≥V(n−r)+w} for every eligible item and n, then every item
  multiset of total rank n has cost≤V(n). Induction on the number of
  items proves this. An attaining predecessor is needed only for
  sharpness, not for an upper bound. Unreachable ranks must be
  represented and verified if present; these completed59 tables contain
  rank1 and hence every rank is reachable.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{ContextCover59}.} Every residual forest is covered by
  the no-context, reserve-one-A1, or reserve-two-A1 branch, with all A2
  multiplicities fixed explicitly and no-A2 residual tables. The old
  charge is \texttt{a2(a2−1)/4} when an A10 and at least two A1 occur;
  the newer charge is \texttt{a2*d5} when an A9 and at least one A1
  occur. Upper guards allow the corresponding rank9/rank10
  representative. If both guards hold, the two-A1 branch includes both
  charges. Presence of several witnesses does not multiply either
  charge.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{FiniteBudget59}.} The complete domain, domination,
  context cover and5148 Bellman certificates prove charge≤6264/16=783/2
  for every finite vertex. This is a representative upper, not an
  asserted exact actual maximum. The representative maximizer has actual
  cost355.5.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{ProductPolynomial}.} For every positive rank list r
  summing to58, \texttt{H=∏(1+…+t\^{}\{r\_i\})},
  \texttt{V=∏(r\_i+1)=Σh\_j} and \texttt{G=Σ\ min(j,58−j)h\_j}. All
  coefficients are positive, symmetric and at least1. The curvature is
  \texttt{(5G−58V)/2} and the envelope is \texttt{V\ Σc(r\_i)}, not
  merely \texttt{Σc(r\_i)}.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{LowNineConcentration}.} If \texttt{1≤a≤b\textless{}9},
  the replacement \texttt{(a,b)→(a−1,b+1)} at fixed total rank increases
  the centered sum of independent discrete uniforms in convex order.
  Therefore it does not increase normalized curvature. Since c(r)=r/2
  for r≤9, it preserves normalized cost. It decreases
  \texttt{(a+1)(b+1)} to \texttt{a(b+2)} and increases the sum of
  squared ranks, so iteration terminates at a profile with at most one
  positive rank below9. Other ranks are not concentrated.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{TerminalIdeal59}.} Every one of the1890 terminal
  profiles has normalized envelope margin≥1/340\textgreater0 and
  absolute envelope surplus≥91/2. This is verified from exact polynomial
  products and rational c(r), with a proof that the profile list is the
  entire terminal domain.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{PositiveSurplusTransfer}.} If
  \texttt{V≥V\textquotesingle{}≥0} and
  \texttt{m≥m\textquotesingle{}\textgreater{}0}, then
  \texttt{Vm≥V\textquotesingle{}m\textquotesingle{}}. Apply this only
  after terminal positivity is established. Together with the
  factor-fiber bound \texttt{C\_actual≤VΣc(r\_i)}, every actual ideal
  vertex has \texttt{κ−C\_actual≥91/2}. Negative terminal margins would
  not permit this argument.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{ShapeCurvature59}.} Let \texttt{D5=Σ\_F(5−s(F))}. The
  local index formula and global minimum/maximum vertices give
  \texttt{D5≥(783/2)v\_f+Σκ(v)+4350}. The extra4350 is counted once. The
  two extrema give \texttt{5\ Σ\_\{j=30\}\^{}\{58\}(2j−58)=5*870}; every
  h coefficient is≥1 for the simplex/product-of-simplices vertex figures
  here.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{PaymentUpper}.} From nonnegative weights and the
  triangle/quad lower totals,
  \texttt{D5≤Σ\ corner\ weights≤(783/2)v\_f+ΣC(v)}. Faces with at least
  five sides have nonpositive deficit and need no positive lower
  payment. This is a finite-sum double-counting theorem.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{Exclude59}.} Subtract the last two inequalities and
  use the cusp surplus: \texttt{0≥4350+(91/2)v\_i\textgreater{}0},
  contradiction. This includes v\_i=0.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{Dimension58}.} \texttt{Exclude59} plus the internally
  proved completed59 tail implies n≤58. It would be incorrect to infer
  the higher tail merely from excluding dimension59 or to assume induced
  faces inherit every required Coxeter/volume property without a
  theorem.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Published mathematical inputs versus internal
proofs}\label{published-mathematical-inputs-versus-internal-proofs}

The external boundary must contain exact statements and hypotheses from
published sources, not names standing for the repository's new results.
The frozen reports identify these primary inputs:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Classification of irreducible finite and affine Coxeter diagrams,
  including the arbitrary-label rank-two families and proper-principal
  definiteness properties.
\item
  Compact Lannér order at most5 and quasi-Lannér order at most10. The
  \href{../results/fresh_high_rank_quasilanner_census_20261017.md}{high-rank
  census} records Chein's primary classification and distinguishes the
  published ceiling from the new146,262-attachment reproduction of26
  diagrams.
\item
  Standard finite-volume cusp-link and simple-at-edges structure, and
  published containment of a parabolic subdiagram in its ideal vertex.
  The repository also gives its own positive-kernel/acute-cone argument.
\item
  Khovanskii's exact incidence reduction and simple-polytope index
  formula (theorems2,6,9 as cited by the shape-curvature report).
\end{itemize}

The stronger4350 correction, factor-fiber payment multiplicity,
convex-order reduction, all current local weights, arbitrary-support
seals, complete native-domain arguments, finite contextual budgets,
positive ideal margin extension and both completed58/59 conclusions are
\textbf{internal}. They must be proved or reduced to checked
certificates; none belongs in an external axiom file merely because it
is lengthy.

\section{Assumption boundary}\label{assumption-boundary}

The user permits published external theorems to be assumed. The registry
in \url{assumptions.json} names those statements separately from
unformalized internal facts. At present the Lean modules use explicit
arguments rather than introducing geometric axioms. For example,
\texttt{defect\_gap\_of\_partition} proves its conclusion from a
selected/rest defect partition; the new geometric construction of that
partition still needs a Lean proof. Likewise the field-composition
theorem does not by itself prove the internally new field-specific
dimension bounds.

Consequently \textbf{none of the complete geometric dimension/volume
theorems is yet labelled end-to-end Lean-verified}. Successful
compilation is genuine verification of the stated module theorems, with
their explicit hypotheses; it is not a substitute for proving the
remaining internal bridges.

The manuscripts and per-result lemma maps document the next obligations.

\chapter{Status of the dimension-163
proof}\label{status-of-the-dimension-163-proof}

The repository contains a \textbf{complete, internally checked
computer-assisted proof} that every finite-sided, finite-volume real
hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has dimension at most163. No unresolved
mathematical step is currently identified in its final reviewed chain.
Arithmeticity, compactness, simple cusps and a bound on the number of
facets are not additional hypotheses.

The authoritative
\href{fresh_nikulin_two_budget_frontier_20261015_dimension163.md}{final
case split} binds the
\href{fresh_nikulin_two_budget_frontier_20261015_review.md}{ordered-budget
argument and independent arithmetic review}, the all-rank estimates and
the inherited geometric proof. The latter has an explicit
\href{fresh_dimension225_hostile_20261015.md}{internal geometric audit},
including actual framing-wall incidence, common cusp-height ratios,
endpoint Schur budgets and the compact-facet alternative. Standard
published narrowness, classification and simple-polytope results are
stated inputs.

The computational portions have exact certificates and separately
implemented checks. The geometric portions have written internal
reviews. These reviews were performed within the agent workflow; they
are not external mathematician refereeing. The proof is not formalized
in Lean or another proof assistant. External validation, publication
priority and current-best literature status remain separate
unestablished matters.

The word \emph{candidate} in frozen historical reports expresses that
validation status; it does not identify a remaining open case or
unproved local inequality. It should not be read as reducing the result
to numerical evidence. Those frozen reports and their hashes are
preserved.

On2026-10-17 the final case/dependency checker was rerun successfully,
checking 30 recursive manifests and83 source files. This rechecks that
package's integrity, exact final inequalities and case split; it does
not rerun every historical calculation or formally verify the geometric
arguments.

\chapter{Independent geometric and literature audit of the Prokhorov
refinement}\label{independent-geometric-and-literature-audit-of-the-prokhorov-refinement}

\textbf{PASS, with a literature-status qualification.} The proposed
upper bound 990 follows from the cited published geometric lemmas and
the new additive diagram estimate. It requires no arithmetic,
compactness, ideal-vertex simplicity, finite-label cutoff, facet count,
or source-chamber restriction. It is an explicit refinement of the
published 995 argument. This review does \textbf{not} establish
publication priority or a new strongest known bound: an older primary
source announces a stronger bound below 300.

The
\href{../scripts/dimension_bound_prokhorov_20261015_proof_review.py}{small
standalone checker} and
\href{dimension_bound_prokhorov_20261015_proof_review.json}{certificate}
bind the \href{dimension_bound_prokhorov_20261015.json}{primary
construction} and
\href{dimension_bound_prokhorov_20261015_review.json}{independent
arithmetic audit}. They check the elementary identities below. The
geometric audit is a source/proof review, not another computerized proof
of the imported topological classification.

\section{Why the edge estimate applies, including at
cusps}\label{why-the-edge-estimate-applies-including-at-cusps}

\href{https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1484&what=fullteng}{Prokhorov's
original paper}, printed pp.~408 and 410, identifies the relevant edge
diagram as elliptic of rank/order (n-1). Its unordered marked-node pairs
determine the three-face angle incidences. Lemma 2 on p.~406 permits any
positive edge constant (C); Proposition 5 supplies the good-face lower
bound. The proposed argument changes only that constant, retaining every
angle weight and all geometric lower bounds.

There is also a direct local explanation. An edge has points in
hyperbolic space even when one or both endpoints are ideal. At a
relative interior point, its incident reflections act on a
positive-definite transverse space of dimension (n-1). Its diagram is
spherical. The affine diagrams at ideal endpoints are different objects;
they must not replace this edge diagram. Edge simplicity gives the local
Boolean interval of containing faces, so deleting an unordered pair of
incident facet constraints selects the corresponding three-face. In
fact, the upper estimate only needs an injection into node pairs.

Consequently there is no omitted affine edge family, cusp multiplicity,
or ordered-pair factor. Distances are ordinary numbers of graph edges,
ignoring labels. Disconnected components contribute no pairs. Unbounded
finite labels occur in (I\_2(m)), whose unlabelled graph is always the
two-node path. The complete finite real Coxeter classification has no
exceptional connected family of unbounded rank beyond paths and (D\_r).

\section{An all-rank argument without a small-diagram
census}\label{an-all-rank-argument-without-a-small-diagram-census}

Put (W=(2f\_7+f\_\{15\})/3), where (f\_k) counts unordered node pairs at
graph distance at most (k). For a path of rank (r\ensuremath{\ge17}),
(f\_k=kr-k(k+1)/2) for (k=7,15). For (D\_r), each of these counts is
larger by one. Thus the deficits (29r-3W) are respectively 176 and 173.

For any component of rank (1\ensuremath{\le }r\ensuremath{\le16}), even
the complete-graph bound suffices:

\[
29r-3W\ge29r-3\binom r2=\frac{r(61-3r)}2\ge\frac{13r}2>0.
\]

For a spherical forest of total rank (N\ensuremath{\ge27}), a large
component already supplies deficit at least 173, while all remaining
deficits are positive. If every component is small, their combined
deficit is at least (13N/2\textgreater173). Hence
(W\ensuremath{\le}(29N-173)/3) for every such forest. This weaker
threshold than the primary's (N\ensuremath{\ge17}) is sufficient for the
dimension theorem, and avoids depending on any finite exceptional-graph
calculation.

For a hypothetical dimension (n\ensuremath{\ge991}), choose the single
positive constant

\[
C=C_n=\frac{29}{3}-\frac{173}{3(n-1)}.
\]

It is uniform over all edges of this polytope. Dependence on the fixed
dimension is permitted. The published lemma yields

\[
n<996-\frac{5536}{n-1},\qquad
n^2-997n+6532<0.
\]

Writing (n=991+t) turns the last polynomial into
(t\^{}2+985t+586\textgreater0), a contradiction for every real
(t\ensuremath{\ge0}). At 990 it equals (-398), so this argument stops at
990. The primary's separate parity calculation agrees; the simpler
substitution already proves the conclusion.

\section{The older 300 announcement must remain
visible}\label{the-older-300-announcement-must-remain-visible}

The official
\href{https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf}{ICM
1986 proceedings} contain Nikulin's \emph{Discrete Reflection Groups in
Lobachevsky Spaces and Algebraic Surfaces}, printed pp.~654--671. His
definition on p.~654 makes CHRG mean finite-covolume reflection groups,
including nonarithmetic groups. Printed p.~659 explicitly asserts
dimension below 300. Pages 657--659 outline a narrow-face method and
work out an affine-(A) cusp example, but do not supply the full
numerical treatment of all diagram types needed to verify the final 300
claim from this text alone. The local audit read the original pages, not
merely a search snippet.

\href{https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga/wp-content/uploads/sites/1334/2024/08/reflections08.pdf}{Dolgachev's
2008 survey}, printed p.~11, explicitly calls that result an
announcement and cites Nikulin. More recent papers still quote 995,
including the
\href{https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-institute-of-mathematics-of-jussieu/article/counting-and-equidistribution-of-strongly-reversible-closed-geodesics-in-negative-curvature/176CFA32FE84C00D6F098FF8D3FCA29F}{2026
paper on strongly reversible geodesics}. This disagreement in citation
practice does not establish that the announcement is false, nor does the
announcement alone constitute an independently checked complete proof
here.

The accurate status is therefore: \textbf{990 is a fully explicit,
independently audited consequence of the stated published Prokhorov
inputs; a stronger historical primary announcement exists, and
priority/current-best status is unresolved.} Recovering the full
narrow-face constants is a substantive next task. No external
announcement should erase that distinction.

For reproducible provenance, the source above was downloaded as the
complete official 974-page first volume. Its PDF pages 756--773 contain
printed pages 654--671; the local review excerpt was extracted from
precisely those pages, without OCR substitutions. The source URL and
page mapping, rather than a transient local path, are the durable
reference.

The missing verification target is concrete: derive uniform explicit
separation inequalities for every irreducible affine cusp type and every
product of affine components, with the possible outgoing edge
completions fully covered. Then compare those bounds with the
narrow-face distance constraint and treat the alternative where the
narrow facet has only finite vertices. The affine-(A) illustration alone
does not establish those omitted cases. This is a proposed
proof-reconstruction task, not an assertion that the announcement cannot
be completed.

\section{Separate conditional compact
audit}\label{separate-conditional-compact-audit}

The geometric argument in the
\href{dimension_bound_lane_20261015.md}{compact-component report} also
passes source/proof review. At a finite vertex, inverse
positive-definite Coxeter Gram blocks count nonright intrinsic two-face
angles, giving the stated average component-pair inequality and the
conditional rank bound (d\ensuremath{\le}4r). This counts all pairs
within each component, not only graph edges.

Its stronger quadrilateral charge requires the full \textbf{flag/3-free}
premise: every empty facet family contains a disjoint pair. Merely
having no triangular two-faces is insufficient. Under that premise,
opposite quadrilateral side facets are globally disjoint. If all
adjacent pairs were right, the four normals would give two negative
directions. Thus one direct spherical-diagram edge can be charged at a
corner, and the corner plus released pair determines the two-face,
making the charge injective. This justifies
(q\_4\ensuremath{\le}\ensuremath{\sum}\_v(d-c(v))) and the conditional
bounds 11 or 10 stated there. The proof uses

\section{Exact cost and complete
maximization}\label{exact-cost-and-complete-maximization}

Let a\_i count A\_i components for1\textless=i\textless=5, put
\texttt{a=sum(i*a\_i)}, let t count D11 through D16, and let
u,b10,b11,b12,b13 count A17,B10,D11,D12,D13. The exact cost of a
representative forest in the upgraded variant is

\begin{verbatim}
sum_components base(type)
  + a*(3t/2+u)
  + a1*b12 + a2*b10 + a4*b13
  + a1*b11.
\end{verbatim}

Omit only the last term for the first variant. The broad three-mark D
half-coupons and two-mark A17 half-coupons give the second term. The
inherited D12 leaf upgrade, A2/B10 halves and A4/D13 neighbor halves
give the next three terms. The new D11 addition has two leaves, each
increased by1/2 against an A1, giving exactly \texttt{a1*b11}. This is
an increment to the existing halves, so the same marked pair is never
counted twice.

Enumerate every count vector of the eight coupon-bearing types
\texttt{B10,D11,D12,D13,D14,D15,D16,A17} with total rank at most75.
There are 1,608 vectors, as in the inherited complete enumeration.
\textbf{D17 is not included in its A17 coordinate.} The residual
additive components have ranks1 through9 or17 through75, represented by
A\_r in the first range and D\_r in the second.

For each fixed large vector, double the costs. A residual rank r has
base \texttt{r*(r-1)} at r\textless=17 and \texttt{16*r-64} at larger r.
At r\textless=5 add \texttt{r*(3t+2u)}, and additionally
\texttt{2*(b12+b11)} for r=1, \texttt{2*b10} for r=2, or \texttt{2*b13}
for r=4. In the first variant set the upgrade coordinate b11 to zero
while retaining D11 in t.

Only \texttt{(t,u,b10,b12,b13,upgraded\_b11)} matters. There are377
tuples in the first variant and675 in the upgraded variant. For every
tuple k, compute all76 Bellman values

\begin{verbatim}
F_k(0)=0,
F_k(s)=max_(allowed r<=s) (F_k(s-r)+weight_k(r)).
\end{verbatim}

This is a complete induction over residual rank: delete any component to
obtain a predecessor, and conversely attach the selected component to an
attaining predecessor. Then maximize the large base plus the appropriate
residual value over all feasible large vectors. Each saved maximum
includes an attaining \textbf{typed} forest, checked by a separate
direct evaluation of the full displayed cost formula. The type labels
ensure an A17 coupon cannot be accidentally assigned to D17.

\section{The precise change}\label{the-precise-change}

A whole A2 has two possible marked roots, and a whole D11 has two short
fork leaves. The four existing half-payments therefore have total cost2.
Making each a unit raises that total to4, an increment of2 for each
A2/D11 component pair. In doubled units this is exactly4a\_2d\_11.

All existing base costs and cross coupons remain. In particular the new
D10 coupons still replace the dominated B10 contribution without adding
it twice; the A1/D11 full upgrade is already present and receives no
further increase. With the predecessor's notation the doubled
representative cross cost becomes

\[
a(2d_{10}+3t+2u)+2a_1(d_{11}+d_{12})+2a_4d_{13}+4a_2d_{11}.
\]

The rank-preserving type-domination comparisons are repeated with this
changed coupon function. Replacing a small rank2 component by A2 can add
the new coupon and cannot lower the cost. Replacing an A11 or other
rank11 component by D11 also remains valid. Thus the same representative
types and complete1,608 large-component multisets apply.

coupon from one half to one. The affine cost becomes62 instead of66. The
other payments are retained paths of length at most5, whole finite
components of order at most17, and inherited finite half-coupons. There
is no arithmeticity, simple-cusp or spectator-rank hypothesis.

dimension consequence remain separate obligations.

\chapter{Four opposite-fork-leaf transfers in affine

Let an actual quadrilateral of a finite-sided finite-volume hyperbolic
Coxeter polytope have a varying affine D12 factor F of order13 at an
ideal corner. If its two marks are short leaves at opposite forks, its
ideal unit may be removed after adding the full finite
whole-A1/whole-D12-short-leaf coupon. The quadrilateral is then paid by
a retained short path, a whole finite component of order at most17, this
new full coupon, or two inherited halves. All four cross-fork-leaf pairs
are covered. There is no arithmetic, simple cusp, facet-count or
spectator-rank restriction.

The
\href{../scripts/fresh_affine_d12_leaf_pair_transfer_20261017.py}{source}
and

verify the exact Schur identities and boundary configurations. The
additional coupon fits the
\href{fresh_finite8_d12_b10_coupon_budget_20261017.md}{joint finite8
budget} through ambient dimension75. This is a universal face-local
transfer, so it also covers the immediate affine-D12 alternatives in
earlier proofs, not only the saved preferred-core contexts. No new
ambient bound is asserted here.

profiles}\label{actual-face-and-complete-profiles}

white diagram and each white-plus-one-black edge diagram are strictly
positive definite. Every adjacent corner is positive semidefinite. At
the chosen ideal corner, W+a+b splits as F plus a positive-definite
spectator diagram Z orthogonal to F. The actual four-black Schur
complement has determinant zero. These properties hold also at a
nonsimple ideal vertex.

Adjacent black contact already gives a path of length1 and a retained
unit. Likewise a shared spectator contact of c and d gives a path of
length2. Assume neither occurs. Thus b.c=a.d=c.d=0, and the nonnegative
native contact vectors x,y of c,d with Z have disjoint supports. The
opposite products a.c and b.d remain unrestricted native products,
including parallel and dotted cases. Every nonzero native magnitude is
at least1; if it exceeds1, it is at least sqrt2.

Number the spine of F as0--1--\ldots--8, with short leaves9,10 at0
and11,12 at8. The marks are a in\{9,10\}, b in\{11,12\}. Give spine
roots cusp coefficient1 and short leaves coefficient1/2. The scaled
affine Gram is a Laplacian, and its resistance between a and b
is8+2+2=12.

Deleting a short leaf leaves finite D12, with its long endpoint the mate
of that leaf and its second node the old fork center. At this rank its

\section{A nonextreme end: the zero boundary seals the
spectators}\label{a-nonextreme-end-the-zero-boundary-seals-the-spectators}

If at least one end is nonextreme, g\_c+g\_d\textless=12. If it is
smaller, the normalized determinant is strictly positive even before the
nonnegative spectator correction, which is impossible. Equality requires
one extreme end of cost8 and one nonextreme end of cost4. The latter is
precisely: isolated with t=sqrt2; mate4 with t=0; or center3 with t=0.

The spectator correction must vanish. Positive definiteness gives
x/h=y/k; their disjoint supports then force x=y=0. Thus every spectator
is orthogonal to F and both new roots, and cannot enlarge a displayed
corner component.

Choose the adjacent corner containing the extreme new root and the old
mark at the opposite end, excluding the nonextreme new root. If the
extreme root was attached to the selected old leaf, that selected leaf
is absent: the new root is a whole A1 and the other mark is a short leaf
of whole D12. This receives the new full coupon. If it was attached to
the mate instead, the long arm extends to whole finite D13, and both
marks receive the old whole-component unit. Adding the orthogonal
positive-definite Z leaves this actual corner finite.

There are48 literal cases: four old mark pairs, two choices of the
extreme profile, three nonextreme equality profiles, and two
orientations. The checker reconstructs every Gram, its
signature(13,1,1), white and edge positivity, all corner
semidefiniteness, and the chosen whole finite components. Doubled bonds
are made rational by scaling only the relevant new root by sqrt2; its
diagonal is4 and its single bond entry is-2. The chosen corner excludes

0=-1/3+D/3,  D=(x-y)^T G_Z^(-1)(x-y),

attaches to the mate, it has whole D13 containing both marks. It is
finite and receives a unit. The case x=0 is reflected. No classification
of the nonzero one-sided contact vector is needed. The32 literal choices
in the checker verify this whole-component statement; their arbitrary
spectator block is handled by the stated orthogonality argument.

The separate augmented diagrams Z+c and Z+d are strictly positive

and D=1, the only possibilities are unit contacts on two distinct whole

any other supporting roots.

is orthogonal to this17-root core. All16 choices of old marks and
attachment leaves have signature(15,1,1); their three new corners are

corresponding adjacent corner has a whole A2 against a short leaf of
whole D12 and receives the inherited half. An attachment to the mate
instead extends the long arm to D14 and receives the old whole-component
unit. The checker gives four cases with two halves, eight with a unit
and one half, and four with three units. Each receives at least one,
with no use of the new full A1 coupon.

This exhausts all possible spectator behavior. Every use of a finite
coupon has established whole actual components, rather than only a
finite subdiagram inside an ideal corner.

\section{Payment interface and

\chapter{Affine distance8 plus feature-near distance9 pair
budget}\label{affine-distance8-plus-feature-near-distance9-pair-budget}

Let D be a connected affine Coxeter diagram with m nodes. Mark as
features every vertex of degree at least3 and both endpoints of every
nonsimple bond (label at least4, including the parallel bond). Give an
unordered pair weight1 if its graph distance is at most8, or if its
distance is9 and at least one endpoint is within14 graph steps of the
feature set. Optionally give every pair weight1 when m≤17. Then the
number P(D) of paid pairs satisfies

\[
P(D)\le\min\{8m,\tbinom m2\}.
\]

The rule is intrinsic under every weighted-diagram automorphism. The
\href{../scripts/fresh_affine_distance8_feature_payment_20261017.py}{source}
and
\href{fresh_affine_distance8_feature_payment_20261017.json}{certificate}
give exact graph counts and verify the formulas below. This is an affine
graph-cost lemma only. It does not prove that the weights pay every
triangle or quadrilateral, and it does not assert dimension97 or any
other new dimension bound.

\section{Small diagrams and
completeness}\label{small-diagrams-and-completeness}

For m≤17, even paying every pair gives binom(m,2)≤8m. Thus the optional
whole-component rule is safe without any further graph assumption. The
certificate additionally checks all63 standard connected affine
catalogue entries of order at most17: affine A1; the available A/B/C/D
families; E6,E7,E8,F4,G2. It records each literal labelled graph and
exact pair-distance histogram.

The standard affine Coxeter classification is an inherited input, as in
the frozen \href{fresh_simple_cusp_distance_bound_20261017.md}{classical
graph-count package} and
\href{fresh_h20_parabolic_endpoint_profiles_20261017.md}{affine endpoint
catalogue}. In orders m≥18 only the classical A/B/C/D families remain.
The finite-rank checks corroborate the arbitrary-rank counting proof
below; they are not a cutoff argument for completeness.

\section{Arbitrary-rank counts}\label{arbitrary-rank-counts}

For m≥18 the exact counts are:

min(9m−44,8m−2) \\

\end{longtable}
}

Every total is at most8m. Since m≥18 implies8m≤binom(m,2), this proves
the asserted budget in these ranks.

For an affine A cycle there are no features. Each distance k=1,\ldots,8
contributes exactly m unordered pairs because2k\textless m. No distance9
pair is added.

For the tree families, number a spine with M vertices by0,\ldots,M−1.
Its short-pair count is sum(k=1,\ldots,8)(M−k)=8M−36. A spine pair at
distance9 is uniquely(i,i+9), with0≤i≤M−10, giving M−9 positions. The
first min(a,L) positions and last min(b,L) positions in a list of length
L have union size min(L,a+b): if disjoint their sizes add, and otherwise
their union is the entire list. This identity also covers a or b larger
than L.

For C the whole graph is the spine, M=m. The doubled terminal bonds
make0,1,M−2,M−1 features. The near-feature vertices satisfy i≤15 or
i≥M−16. Therefore a distance9 pair(i,i+9) is added exactly when i≤15 or
i≥M−25: the first16 and last16 positions. This gives min(m−9,32) extras.

For B, M=m−2 and two simple leaves are attached to the left spine
endpoint0. The far spine bond(M−2,M−1) is doubled, so the features
are0,M−2,M−1. Near-feature spine vertices satisfy i≤14 or i≥M−16. A
distance9 spine pair is added when i≤14 or i≥M−25: the first15 and
last16 positions, giving min(m−11,31). Each of the two left leaves adds
its pair with spine vertex8, for two more distance9 pairs. At
distances≤8 the leaves contribute16 leaf-spine pairs and one leaf-leaf
pair, hence8M−36+16+1=8m−35.

For D, M=m−4 and two simple leaves attach to each spine endpoint. The
features are0 and M−1. Near-feature spine vertices satisfy i≤14 or
i≥M−15. A distance9 spine pair is added when i≤14 or i≥M−24: the first15
and last15 positions, giving min(m−13,30). The four leaves each have one
distance9 pair along the spine, adding4. Opposite-end leaf pairs have
distance M+1≥15 and contribute neither short nor extra payment. At
distances≤8 the leaves contribute32 leaf-spine pairs and two same-end
leaf-leaf pairs, hence8M−36+32+2=8m−34.

The deficits from8m are max(45−m,4), max(44−m,2) and max(43−m,0),
respectively. Affine D therefore attains equality for every m≥43. The
radius14 is sharp for this uniform rule: radius15 on affine D of
order100 pays802 pairs, exceeding800. This diagnostic is also checked
exactly.

Dividing the bound by m gives the per-factor form P(D)/m≤min(8,(m−1)/2).
Applying it to actual cusp incidence multiplicities requires the
separate geometric counting argument; no transfer is inferred merely
from this graph estimate.

\section{What the sensitivities mean}\label{what-the-sensitivities-mean}

A component-base decrease d contributes d times the number of those
components. A decrease q in an ordinary \textbf{total component-pair
cost} contributes q times the number of those unordered component pairs.
A per-small-mark decrease delta against D15 contributes

\begin{verbatim}
delta * (3*c3+4*c4+5*c5) * cD15,
\end{verbatim}

where cr counts all whole components of rank r, across their actual
finite types. The source checks that their present D15 component-pair
cost is3r/2 for every actual type of rank3,4 or5. That aggregate
identity does not prove which individual geometric coupon role can be
decreased.

For example, lowering one intrinsic D15 fork-center role from1/2 to3/8
for every small rank3--5 mark would have the measured delta=1/8 effect,
\textbf{if} a complete proof preserves every use of that role. Reducing
the two short-leaf roles by1/16 each would have the same aggregate cost
but is a different geometric proposal. Neither proposal is asserted
valid here; the center and leaf obligations must be audited separately.

Every recorded witness currently has zero contextual charge. This fact
is checked exactly, but does not mean the contextual rules can be
removed from a future complete count: other forests can trigger them.
Any new compensation must be included before claiming an improved
maximum.

The individual features and grouped features are separate, sometimes
overlapping parameterizations. Their reported savings are not a menu of
independent coupons that may be added without checking overlap. A
component-pair cost unit is not automatically one marked-pair weight;
component rank, diagram symmetry and orbit size determine that
conversion.

\section{Absolute surplus and a stronger global
constant}\label{absolute-surplus-and-a-stronger-global-constant}

The absolute surplus V*m has minimum445/23, attained by the single
rank64 profile. This lower bound also applies before concentration.
Indeed, for 0\textless a\textless=b and a positive allowed transfer
delta,

\begin{verbatim}
(a+1)(b+1)-(a-delta+1)(b+delta+1)
  = delta*(b-a+delta) > 0.
\end{verbatim}

Thus V decreases under every concentration, with a vanished factor
having value1. Normalized margin also decreases, and its terminal value
is positive. Their product consequently decreases. The minimum over the
terminal domain bounds the absolute surplus for every actual cusp.

The \href{fresh_cusp_link_shape_curvature_20261017.md}{shape-curvature
theorem} has a quantitative extremum argument that admits a sharper
constant here, and in fact for all the same finite-volume Coxeter
polytopes. At every vertex figure, finite or ideal, H is a product of
polynomials 1+t+\ldots+t\^{}r, so every coefficient h\_j
for0\textless=j\textless=d is at least1. Its proof gives

\begin{verbatim}
E-G = sum_(j>d/2) h_j*(2j-d)
    >= sum_(j>d/2)(2j-d)
    = floor((d+1)^2/4).
\end{verbatim}

At each of the two distinct global extrema the cutting hyperplane misses
the entire vertex figure, giving E rather than G uncut edges. Their
combined extra contribution to D5 is therefore at least
5*floor(n\^{}2/4), strengthening the earlier5(n-1). No new geometric
hypothesis is needed. At n=65 this constant is5280.

\section{The resulting theorem and remaining finite
obstruction}\label{the-resulting-theorem-and-remaining-finite-obstruction}

Write v\_f and v\_i for the numbers of finite and ideal vertices. The
compatible triangle/quadrilateral payment theorem gives

\begin{verbatim}
D5 <= 487*v_f + sum_(ideal v) V_v*sum_i c(r_vi).
\end{verbatim}

The strengthened shape inequality gives

\begin{verbatim}
D5 >= 480*v_f + sum_(ideal v) (5G_v-64V_v)/2 + 5280.
\end{verbatim}

Combining them with the absolute ideal surplus proves the necessary
dimension65 inequality

\begin{verbatim}
7*v_f >= 5280 + (445/23)*v_i.
\end{verbatim}

In particular, v\_f=0 is impossible. The completed
\href{fresh_ideal5_weighted_dimension65_20261017.md}{unrestricted
ceiling65} already excludes dimensions66 and higher, so the all-ideal
ceiling is64. The same inequality requires at least755 finite vertices
in any remaining dimension65 example, or at least758 if it has an ideal
vertex. These are necessary conditions, not claims that such examples
exist.

There is no upper bound on v\_f in this argument. In particular the
inequality does not eliminate dimension65 in general. The formal finite
forest D17+3D16 still costs487 against480. Arithmeticity, simplicity of
cusps and a facet-count bound are not assumptions of the all-ideal
result. No new finite-volume example or arithmetic dimension bound
follows.

\chapter{A finite local target for the compact dimension-29
problem}\label{a-finite-local-target-for-the-compact-dimension-29-problem}

Any hypothetical compact hyperbolic Coxeter polytope in dimension 29
must have a vertex in an explicit list of \textbf{2,126 spherical
Coxeter forests}, with only nine possible component-rank partitions.
This is an unconditional necessary condition: no arithmetic,
facet-count, or nerve assumption is imposed. It is \textbf{not an
exclusion of dimension 29} and is not a classification of full
polytopes.

The \href{../scripts/fresh_compact_dimension_bound_20261015.py}{exact
checker} and \href{fresh_compact_dimension_bound_20261015.json}{saved
certificate} enumerate the complete local list. They check graph
weights, integer partitions and the combinatorial identity below. A
\href{fresh_compact_dimension_bound_20261015_review.md}{separate
independent review} reproduces the h-vector arithmetic and9/2,126/1,354
counts, and checks the occurrence argument. It inherits the connected
graph weights after source review instead of repeating the66-graph
census. The spherical-diagram classification and the global planar-face
inequality remain published theorem inputs.

The unrestricted compact upper bound remains 29 in the checked primary
survey, \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2109.06758}{Lee--Marquis, Theorem
3.10 and Remark 3.12}. Alexandrov's stronger bound 12 concerns the
additional hypothesis that every missing face has size 2; it does not
exclude general compact dimension 29.
\href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.07248}{Alexandrov, Theorem C and §4}.

\section{The exact combinatorial threshold is
84}\label{the-exact-combinatorial-threshold-is-84}

Use Vinberg's planar-angle weights. For a vertex v write σ(v) for its
total weight, and for a k-gonal two-face F write σ(F) for the sum at its
corners. The published construction has σ(v)≤3n and σ(F)≥5−k. Its
componentwise weights and face proof are in the original
\href{https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=mmo&option_lang=rus&paperid=444&what=fullt}{Vinberg
paper, §§1 and 6, printed pp.70--72 and 80--91}.

For n=29, every vertex lies on 406 two-faces. The exact odd-dimensional
average-side bound is 116/28=29/7. Consequently f₂\textgreater98f₀, and

\[
\sum_v\sigma(v)\ge5f_2-406f_0>84f_0.
\]

Thus a universally valid weighting with vertex bound 84 would suffice.
This is a less demanding numerical target than substituting c=23/8 into
the coarser formula n\textless8c+6. Existing Vinberg weights give 87, so
the outstanding gap is three units per vertex in a uniform bound, or an
appropriate global averaged inequality.

There is an exact version of this comparison. Let h₀,\ldots,h₂₉ be the
h-vector of the dual simplicial polytope; hᵢ=h₂₉₋ᵢ, hᵢ≥0 and h₀=1. The
standard face-count identities give

\[
 f_2-98f_0=\sum_{i=0}^{14}(14-i)(15-i)h_i.
\]

Define s(F)=σ(F)−(5−k\_F)≥0. Double-counting planar angles gives the
exact balance

\[
\boxed{\quad
\sum_v(\sigma(v)-84)
=5\sum_{i=0}^{14}(14-i)(15-i)h_i+\sum_Fs(F).
\quad}
\]

Its right side is at least 1050 using h₀ alone. Because σ(v)≤87, at
least 350 vertices must have σ(v)\textgreater84. This modest lower count
uses no additional h-vector theorem. The certificate checks all 15
coefficients of the identity.

There is a necessary occurrence refinement. Set every angle weight on a
face with five or more sides to zero, retaining the original weights on
triangles and quadrilaterals. Denote the new vertex total by σₛ(v). All
face inequalities remain valid: on a larger face the new total is0≥5−k.
Also σₛ(v)≤σ(v)≤87. The same balance therefore forces at least 350
vertices with σₛ(v)\textgreater84. \textbf{At least one listed extremal
corner has more than 84 units of weight on its incident triangles and
quadrilaterals.} This supplies the small-face occurrence premise;
extremal vertex existence alone would not supply it.

\section{Complete enumeration of the extremal vertex
types}\label{complete-enumeration-of-the-extremal-vertex-types}

Let w(r) be the contribution of an irreducible spherical component of
rank r, and δ(r)=3r−w(r). The result of applying the published weighting
is independent of the irreducible type at fixed rank:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lrr@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Rank & w(r) & δ(r) \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
1 & 0 & 3 \\
2 & 2 & 4 \\
3 & 6 & 3 \\
4 & 12 & 0 \\
5 & 10 & 5 \\
6 & 15 & 3 \\
7 & 21 & 0 \\
8 & 24 & 0 \\
9 & 27 & 0 \\
r≥10 & r+19 & 2r−19 \\
\end{longtable}
}

For the classical A/B/D graphs the checker constructs every relevant end
segment of order at most 6 and counts the union of its node pairs with
adjacent pairs. It directly checks 66 graphs of ranks 8 through 29. At
ranks 8 through 12 it also checks the end-segment list against a
separate exhaustive connected-subset definition. For D, invariance under
swapping the two fork leaves is enforced. The E₈ contribution 28−4=24 is
an explicit published input; the checker does not independently
reconstruct the four pictured exceptional pairs or repeat Vinberg's face
proof.

Since a rank 29 forest has σ=87−Σδ, the strict inequality
σ\textgreater84 requires Σδ≤2. All components therefore have ranks
4,7,8,9 or 10; there can be at most two rank 10 components. Exhausting
all 4,565 partitions of 29 leaves exactly the following list.

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter

}

The available irreducible types are A₄/B₄/D₄/F₄/H₄; A₇/B₇/D₇/E₇;
A₈/B₈/D₈/E₈; and A/B/D in ranks 9 and 10. Repeated equal-rank components
are unordered. The certificate saves every typed forest, rather than
only these counts. B and C are the same unoriented Coxeter type here.

No angle-label cutoff was used. Every finite I₂(m), including
arbitrarily large m, has deficit 4 and therefore cannot occur in an
extremal forest. In fact all extremal vertices use only labels 3,4,5. Of
the 2,126 types, 385 contain E₇, 245 contain E₈ and 772 contain H₄.

\section{A known obstruction to the most obvious
optimization}\label{a-known-obstruction-to-the-most-obvious-optimization}

Vinberg explicitly warns in §6.12, printed p.91, that a uniform
improvement c\textless3 is obstructed when nonnegative weights depend
only on the planar-angle diagram and vanish across its components. E₇
supplies the obstruction through quadrilateral stars. This is a
published limitation of that local architecture, not a new theorem
proved by this checker. It must not be ignored when setting up a
reweighting program.
\href{https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=mmo&option_lang=rus&paperid=444&what=fullt}{Original
remark}.

A rank 29-specific weighting depending on the full forest, weights
across components, or a global charge argument requires separate
analysis; the remark alone is not being promoted into an impossibility
theorem for all such strategies. The exact balance above provides a
test: any proposed global charge must control its positive vertex excess
while retaining the nonnegative face slacks.

Our \href{fresh_h9_lorentz_inertia_20261015.md}{Lorentz-inertia ledger}
supplies valid forbidden configurations in arbitrary Lorentz dimension
only under their literal spherical-face and contact premises. The
strongest high-label configurations are not present inside the extremal
vertices, whose components have no label ≥7. They cannot simply be
declared unavoidable by increasing dimension.

\section{Concrete next verification
target}\label{concrete-next-verification-target}

The 2,126 forests are finite entry points for an exhaustive local
analysis. They are not by themselves a finite algorithm deciding every
chamber completion. For each forest T and each pair of its nodes, delete
those nodes to form a rank 27 white diagram W. A triangular or
quadrilateral two-face through that angle introduces respectively one or
two further black nodes.

The occurrence refinement gives a particularly small certificate target.
If the original vertex weight is W∈\{85,86,87\}, a vertex with
σₛ\textgreater84 can lose at most W−85 units to larger faces. Thus it
suffices, for \textbf{each} listed type, to prove that some marked pairs
of total original weight at least W−84 cannot occur on triangles or
quadrilaterals. The required blocked weight is respectively 1, 2 or3. A
pair of weight2 counts twice. This is an exhaustive marked-angle
coverage requirement, rather than a claim that one arbitrary failed
extension eliminates a corner type.

The necessary conditions can be stated exactly before any numerical
search:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Each adjacent pair of black nodes, together with W, gives a
  positive-definite rank 29 vertex diagram. Each single black node
  together with W is also positive definite.
\item
  After taking the Schur complement of W, a triangular star has a 3×3
  residual of Lorentz signature (2,1). A quadrilateral star has a 4×4
  residual of rank 3 and signature (2,1,0); the opposite black pairs
  give indefinite residual pairs. All full-star principal subdiagrams
  must have negative index at most one, and compactness excludes
  parabolic subdiagrams.
\item
  Every discrete label and continuous dotted distance must remain
  covered. New rank-two spherical factors can arise after deletion, even
  though the original extremal forest has none; such I₂(m) tails cannot
  be truncated without proof.
\end{enumerate}

These conditions give the appropriate interface for the universal
inertia obstructions. Rejecting all small-face extensions for every type
would suffice; more economically, the blocked-weight coverage just
described would exclude compact dimension 29. Alternatively, an exact
charge or modified-weight certificate satisfying every retained
triangle/quadrilateral constraint could contradict the balance identity.
\textbf{Neither rejection nor that global certificate has yet been
produced.} Merely verifying a local corner Gram, or rejecting a bounded
selection of extension labels, would not achieve the goal.

\section{Separate arithmetic
refinement}\label{separate-arithmetic-refinement}

For compact arithmetic groups in dimension at least 22, the relevant
ground-field candidates are Q(√2), Q(√5), and Q(cos(2π/7)); this is a
separate hypothesis from the unconditional reduction.
\href{https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=mmo&option_lang=rus&paperid=444&what=fullt}{Vinberg,
Theorem 2 and §7}.

An H₄ component contains a label 5 edge. Its length-two cyclic product
gives 4cos²(π/5)=(3+√5)/2, so its ground field must contain √5. Q(√2)
does not contain √5, and the degree-three field Q(cos(2π/7)) has no
quadratic subfield. Therefore those two arithmetic cases retain only the
1,354 H₄-free extremal forests. Q(√5) retains all 2,126 at this stage.
Labels 4 in B/F components have rational squared cosine and are not
removed by this argument. No arithmetic lattice or chamber
classification is claimed.

\chapter{Cusp-factor payments and a positive-semidefinite spectator
lemma}\label{cusp-factor-payments-and-a-positive-semidefinite-spectator-lemma}

This package proves a restricted factor-weighted dimension inequality
and an exact Schur-complement monotonicity lemma. The restriction is
essential: \textbf{every irreducible affine factor at every cusp has
rank at least9}. Under that restriction, at most two factors per cusp
imply dimension at most117. This does not improve the unrestricted
bound163. The determinant lemma is intended to support a finer argument
without discarding nonsimple cusps.

The
\href{../scripts/fresh_cusp_factor_payment_framework_20261017.py}{checker}
and \href{fresh_cusp_factor_payment_framework_20261017.json}{saved data}
certify the exact algebra below. Finite graph/model checks corroborate
the all-rank proofs; they do not supply a cutoff argument.

\section{Cusp factors and actual two-face
corners}\label{cusp-factors-and-actual-two-face-corners}

Let P be a finite-sided finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytope of
dimension n.~Write an ideal vertex diagram as a disjoint union of
irreducible affine diagrams with ranks r\_vi, where sum\_i r\_vi=n−1.
Its Euclidean link is the product L\_v=product\_i Delta\^{}(r\_vi). Put

\texttt{s\_v\ =\ number\ of\ factors,\ \ \ \ \ \ \ V\_v\ =\ product\_i\ (r\_vi+1).}

Thus V\_v is the number of edges at v and the link has (n−1)V\_v/2
edges. These are the standard finite-volume cusp-link and
simplicity-at-edges facts used by
\href{https://www.math.utoronto.ca/askold/1986-Faa-1-english.pdf}{Khovanskii,
§6 and Theorem10}, also recorded in the
\href{fresh_finite_volume_simplex_truncation_20261017.md}{frozen
truncation note}.

Every connected affine subdiagram is an entire irreducible factor of its
actual cusp. Indeed its positive kernel gives a nonzero null vector:
pairing its positive root combination with a strict chamber center is
negative. Acuteness makes that vector feasible against every other wall.
A feasible ideal point is extreme in the projective closure, by strict
convexity of the closed Klein ball, hence is an ideal vertex. Its affine
subdiagram lies in one irreducible cusp component, whose proper
principal subdiagrams are positive definite. The published containment
of every parabolic subdiagram in its unique ideal vertex diagram appears
in \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0502413}{Felikson--Tumarkin, §1}.

An actual two-face has an elliptic supporting set W of n−2 walls. Each
of its edges adds one side normal, giving a positive-definite set of n−1
walls because the edge has an interior hyperbolic point. At an ideal
corner, the corresponding link edge varies in exactly one simplex factor
i. W retains r\_vi−1 nodes in that factor and r\_vj nodes in every other
factor. Adding its two marked sides restores the full affine factor i;
all other factors have one node deleted and are elliptic. In particular
the marked pair lies in the varying factor. Every pair of nodes of
factor i occurs in exactly V\_v/(r\_vi+1) such link-edge fibers.

This description does not assume that the cusp itself is simple. An
independent internal conceptual read checked this corner/fiber
multiplicity and the closed-edge argument below; it did not repeat the
scalar or graph checks.

\section{A restricted distance-seven payment
theorem}\label{a-restricted-distance-seven-payment-theorem}

Assume from now on that every r\_vi\textgreater=9. There is no affine
subdiagram of order at most9. A minimal indefinite diagram is Lannér or
quasi-Lannér of order at most10; the quasi-Lannér case contains an
affine proper subdiagram of order at most9 and is therefore excluded.
Every minimal indefinite diagram is consequently Lannér of order at
most5. The finite classification and its use here are inherited
explicitly from the
\href{fresh_simple_cusp_affine_exclusion_20261017.md}{affine-exclusion
proof}.

Assign a two-face corner weight1 when its two side nodes are at graph
distance at most7, and weight0 otherwise. For a triangle, a minimal
indefinite subdiagram of its star contains all three sides. Its order is
at most5. A tree joining the three marked nodes has at least two
marked-to-marked paths avoiding the third node, each of length at most3;
these give two paid corners. Cyclic minimal diagrams only supply
additional short paths. Thus every triangle receives at least2.

For a quadrilateral, W plus either opposite pair is indefinite. If it
were positive definite, the usual acute projection of the strict center
would give a point on both opposite closed sides. If it were positive
semidefinite and singular, its positive affine kernel would give a
nonzero feasible ideal point on both opposite closed sides. Both
contradict their disjointness, including when the quadrilateral has
ideal vertices. Let L and M be minimal indefinite subdiagrams for the
two opposite pairs. Each contains both of its marked nodes, has order at
most5, and has distance at most3 from a white node to a nearest marked
node. The two subdiagrams cannot be orthogonal, because that would give
two negative directions. Their overlap or a joining bond therefore
supplies a path of length at most3+1+3=7 between adjacent sides,
avoiding the other two marked nodes. Every quadrilateral receives at
least1. This is the small-core proof of the frozen distance theorem,
using only actual edge/corner supports rather than simple ideal
vertices.

At a finite vertex the total weight is at most7n. At an ideal vertex, a
factor of order m=r+1\textgreater=10 is classical, and its number of
pairs at distance at most7 is at most7m. The all-rank path, cycle,
single-fork and double-fork formulas are proved in the
\href{fresh_simple_cusp_distance_bound_20261017.md}{distance package}.
The current checker verifies the245 inherited literal graph rows and
their source hashes; these checks are not the justification for
arbitrary rank. Multiplying by the fiber count yields the exact budget

\texttt{C(v)\ \textless{}=\ sum\_i\ {[}V\_v/(r\_vi+1){]}\ *\ 7(r\_vi+1)\ =\ 7\ s\_v\ V\_v.}

\section{The exact weighted
inequality}\label{the-exact-weighted-inequality}

Let v\_f count finite vertices and define

\texttt{beta\_n\ =\ n(n−6)/8\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ (n\ even),}

\texttt{beta\_n\ =\ (n−1)(n−5)/8\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ (n\ odd).}

For the original polytope, not its truncation, Khovanskii's reduction
yields a strict average-face bound for a bounded polytope simple at
edges, as justified immediately below, and gives

\texttt{D5\ =\ sum\_(two-faces\ F)\ (5−number\_of\_sides(F))}

\texttt{\textgreater{}\ beta\_n\ v\_f\ +\ (beta\_n/n)\ sum\_v\ V\_v.}

Here the total two-face/vertex incidence is binom(n,2)v\_f+(n−1)sum\_v
V\_v/2. Here is the strictness step rather than a tacit upgrade of the
published weak bound. Choose a generic linear function on the bounded
projective polytope. For each vertex w, let E\_w be the number of edges
in its simple vertex figure and E\_w\^{}0 the number of those edges not
cut by the hyperplane through w parallel to a level hyperplane. Theorem9
gives the exact identities I=sum\_w E\_w and2f2=sum\_w E\_w\^{}0.
Theorem8, as applied in Theorem10, gives2E\_w/E\_w\^{}0\textless=eta\_n,
where eta\_n=4(n−1)/(n−2) for even n and4n/(n−1) for odd n.~All
denominators are positive. At a global minimum vertex the cutting
hyperplane misses the vertex figure, so E\_w\^{}0=E\_w and this ratio
is2\textless eta\_n.~Thus I/f2, the positively weighted average of these
local ratios, is strictly less than eta\_n.~This proves the displayed
strict lower bound for D5=5f2−I. The argument applies to the bounded
projective closure, including ideal vertices. The checker verifies the
resulting coefficient identities and parity expressions. The corner
payments give

\texttt{D5\ \textless{}=\ 7n\ v\_f\ +\ 7\ sum\_v\ s\_v\ V\_v.}

Consequently

\texttt{beta\_n/(7n)\ \textless{}\ {[}n\ v\_f\ +\ sum\_v\ s\_v\ V\_v{]}\ /\ {[}n\ v\_f\ +\ sum\_v\ V\_v{]}.}

This is the proved factor-weighted inequality. If every s\_v\textless=s,
the right side is at most s, and hence n\textless=56s+5. At N=56s+6,
beta\_N=7sN, which the strict inequality excludes without any additional
finite-vertex assumption. The all-rank threshold check is

\texttt{8(beta\_(N+2t)−7s(N+2t))\ =\ 4t\^{}2+2Nt,}

\texttt{8(beta\_(N+1+2t)−7s(N+1+2t))\ =\ 4t\^{}2+(2N+4)t+N+6.}

Thus the rank-at-least9, at-most-two-factor class has n\textless=117.
These are restricted consequences, not claims about arbitrary
finite-volume polytopes. The frozen all-simple bound29 is already
stronger for s=1.

\section{Orthogonal positive-definite spectators improve a scalar
contradiction}\label{orthogonal-positive-definite-spectators-improve-a-scalar-contradiction}

The following identity has no factor-rank restriction. After eliminating
the supporting whites of an affine marked corner, suppose
alpha\textgreater0 and h,k are nonzero, and its four-root Schur matrix
is

\begin{verbatim}
[ alpha  −alpha   B−h   −A  ]
[−alpha   alpha  −B     A−k ]
[ B−h     −B      C     −E  ]
[−A        A−k   −E      D  ].
\end{verbatim}

Its determinant is

\texttt{(hk−kB−hA)\^{}2\ −\ alpha(Ck\^{}2+Dh\^{}2+2Ehk).}

Additional elliptic white spectators orthogonal to the old affine factor
may couple to the two new roots c,d.~Eliminating them subtracts a
positive-semidefinite matrix {[}{[}p,q{]},{[}q,r{]}{]} from the c,d
block, so C becomes C−p, D becomes D−r and E becomes E+q. With u=1/h and
v=1/k, the normalized determinant changes by

\texttt{alpha(pu\^{}2−2quv+rv\^{}2)\ =\ alpha\ \textbar{}\textbar{}u\ z\_c−v\ z\_d\textbar{}\textbar{}\^{}2\ \textgreater{}=\ 0.}

The equality uses any Gram realization of that positive-semidefinite
correction; h,k are unchanged. Therefore every strict positive
determinant contradiction of this form survives such spectator
attachments. For an actual quadrilateral the complete supporting set has
n−2 independent roots and the four residual normals lie in a Lorentz
three-space, so the determinant must vanish. This explains why a strict
scalar contradiction still excludes the configuration after the
spectators are restored.

This identity transfers scalar portions of the
\href{fresh_simple_cusp_affine_a_quadrilateral_20261017.md}{affine-cycle
proof} and
\href{fresh_simple_cusp_affine_tree_completion_20261017.md}{affine-tree
proof}. It does not itself transfer their entire payment theorem. A
generic finite-component payment can change upon extension (for example,
an abstract E7 diagram embeds in E8), while role-compatible spectator
extensions in the actual proof require a separate literal check. This
sentence does not assert that the specific D6-to-E7 configuration admits
such an extension through its permitted new-root position. Also, a small
affine diagram that was forbidden under simple cusps can now be a
genuine cusp factor. Those separate cases require a new argument before
a3s\_v V\_v budget can be asserted.

\section{Two factors do not force absence of small affine
diagrams}\label{two-factors-do-not-force-absence-of-small-affine-diagrams}

There is an exact local cusp model in every dimension m+1,
m\textgreater=3, with link Delta\^{}1 times Delta\^{}(m−1). It shows why
a factor-count hypothesis alone cannot replace the minimum-rank
hypothesis above.

Use a Lorentz space with null nu,eta satisfying nu.eta=−1, an orthogonal
unit e, and an orthogonal A\_(m−1) root system
alpha\_1,\ldots,alpha\_(m−1). Put theta=sum alpha\_i. The normals are

\texttt{e,\ nu−e;\ alpha\_1,...,alpha\_(m−1),\ nu−theta.}

The two components are affine A1 and affine A\_(m−1), mutually
orthogonal, and both positive null relations sum to nu. Their Gram rank
is m and their normal-span rank is m+1. A strict timelike center is

\texttt{H=m\ nu+eta−e/2−sum\_(i=1)\^{}(m−1)\ {[}i(m−i)/(2m){]}\ alpha\_i.}

Its products with the first pair are−1/2 and with each remaining
normal−1/m, while

\texttt{H\^{}2=−2m+1/4+(m\^{}2−1)/(12m)\textless{}0.}

The horospherical link is the bounded product of the two standard
alcoves. These formulas prove the all-rank local realization;22 exact
matrix checks corroborate them. No finite-volume completion in arbitrary
dimension is claimed.

\chapter{A sharp finite-ended cusp-port bound for one- and two-ideal
triangles}\label{a-sharp-finite-ended-cusp-port-bound-for-one--and-two-ideal-triangles}

Let P be a finite-sided, finite-volume acute hyperbolic Coxeter
n-polytope. Write T\_j for the number of triangular two-faces with
exactly j ideal vertices. At an ideal vertex v write its combinatorial
link as

\[
 L_v=\prod_{i=1}^{s_v}\Delta^{r_{vi}},\qquad
 a_v=\#\{\text{edges from v to a finite vertex}\},\qquad
 R_5(v)=\sum_i\min(r_{vi},5).
\]

Let T\_j(v) count those triangles through v. Then

\[
 \boxed{T_1(v)+T_2(v)\le a_vR_5(v)},\qquad
 \boxed{T_1+2T_2\le\sum_{v\ \mathrm{ideal}}a_vR_5(v)}.       \tag{1}
\]

In particular, if every ideal vertex is simple, then

\[
 \boxed{T_1+2T_2\le5E_{fi}}.                              \tag{2}
\]

The constant5 in (2), and the uniform per-factor constant used in (1),
are attained by the classical finite-volume H9 simplex L24. No new
dimension bound or new hyperbolic example is claimed. For nonsimple
cusps, the factor sum in (1) is essential to this proof and is not
replaced by5.

\section{Factor faces and the valid completion
argument}\label{factor-faces-and-the-valid-completion-argument}

A port at v is an old edge through v, hence a vertex of L\_v. Color it
finite or ideal according to its other endpoint. An old two-face through
v gives an edge of L\_v. Every edge of a product of simplices varies in
one factor, so it lies in a unique maximal simplex factor fiber F.
Fixing the other factor coordinates makes F a simplex Delta\^{}\{r\_i\}.
The face correspondence for vertex links gives an actual (r\_i+1)-face
P\_F of P with link F at v. Thus \textbf{v is simple in P\_F}, even if
it is nonsimple in P. Every finite vertex of P\_F is also simple.

These local facts for general finite-volume acute chambers are recorded
in
\href{https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/43032}{Potyagailo--Vinberg,
printed p.64}. They do not say that arbitrary induced faces have Coxeter
angles. The argument below is combinatorial; its later simplex-size
restrictions come from the original-wall-star lemmas, not from treating
P\_F as a Coxeter polytope in its own right.

Fix a finite-ended port va within F. Suppose vab and vac are triangular
faces. The three ports generate a three-face G of P\_F. The vertices v
and a are simple in G and each already has the three neighbors among
v,a,b,c.~If G had another vertex, deleting b,c would disconnect \{v,a\}
from it. This contradicts
\href{https://msp.org/pjm/1961/11-2/pjm-v11-n2-p03-s.pdf}{Balinski's
three-connectivity theorem, printed p.432}. Thus G is a tetrahedron. In
particular vbc is triangular, regardless of whether b,c are finite or
nonsimple ideal vertices elsewhere in P\_F.

All triangular neighbors of the chosen port consequently form a clique.
Let that clique together with va have k ports and generate the k-face A.
Only v and a need be simple: both already have degree k among the k+1
displayed vertices. If A contained any further vertex, deletion of the
other k−1 displayed vertices would disconnect \{v,a\}. Balinski's
k-connectivity excludes this. Therefore A is the whole k-simplex. This
also handles k=2 directly as the initial triangle; k=1 has no triangle
contribution.

These maximal simplex blocks \textbf{within the fixed fiber} have
disjoint sets of finite-ended ports. Indeed, if two blocks shared such a
port, the preceding completion applied to all its triangular neighbors
would merge them. They may share ideal-ended ports. Every triangle
through v with at least one other finite vertex belongs to exactly one
such block. The two types counted are T\_1(v) and T\_2(v).

No maximality in the ambient face poset is required when applying the
frozen ideal-count classification: it bounds \textbf{every actual
simplex face}, including these fiber-maximal blocks. No degree assertion
is made about their undisplayed ideal neighbors.

\section{The coefficient calculation}\label{the-coefficient-calculation}

In one block let f\textgreater=1 be its number of finite-ended ports and
i\textgreater=0 its number of ideal-ended ports. The block simplex has
dimension k=f+i, with f finite vertices and i+1 ideal vertices, because
v itself is ideal. Its contribution is exactly

\[
 T_1(v;A)+T_2(v;A)=\binom f2+fi
       =f\left({f-1\over2}+i\right).                     \tag{3}
\]

The \href{fresh_multi_ideal_triangle_scope_20261017.md}{original-star
theorem} gives k\textless=9. The
\href{fresh_finite_edge_cusp_tradeoff10_20261017.md}{seven-simplex
theorem} allows at most three ideals or all eight vertices ideal; the
latter case is excluded here by f\textgreater=1. The
\href{fresh_finite_edge_cusp_tradeoff12_20261017.md}{eight- and
nine-simplex bounds} give at most three ideals as well. Hence for
k\textgreater=7, i\textless=2 and

\[
 {f-1\over2}+i={k+i-1\over2}\le5.
\]

For k\textless=6 the same expression is at most k−1\textless=5. Thus the
new coefficient does not require extending the six-simplex theorem to
the unproved one-finite/six-ideal case. That case, with f=1,i=5, is
explicitly retained in the exact checker. Also k\textless=r\_i+1 inside
this factor face, so the expression is at most r\_i. Consequently each
block contributes at most f*min(r\_i,5).

Sum over the disjoint finite-port sets in a fiber. For any one factor i,
each finite-ended port of the full link belongs to exactly one fiber of
that factor. Summing over all fibers therefore contributes at most
a\_v*min(r\_i,5), and then summing over factors proves the local bound
in (1). A T\_1 triangle is counted at one cusp and a T\_2 triangle at
two; this gives the global identity and inequality. Finally sum\_v
a\_v=E\_fi. A simple cusp has one factor, proving (2).

The
\href{../scripts/fresh_cusp_finite_port_triangle_capacity_20261017.py}{standalone
Fraction checker} enumerates all28 allowed (k,f,i) types under the
inherited safe envelopes, and verifies the coefficient formula. The
checks through factor rank64 only confirm the explicit all-rank argument
above; no rank cutoff is used in its proof. Formal maximizing types are
not asserted realizable.

\section{Sharpness and the previous
counterexample}\label{sharpness-and-the-previous-counterexample}

The \href{fresh_finite_edge_cusp_tradeoff_28over3_20261017.md}{literal
L24 certificate} already proves that this rational Gram defines a
finite-volume H9 Coxeter simplex with seven finite and three ideal
vertices. Its full geometry was also checked by the
\href{review_finite_edge_28over3_20261017.md}{independent Fraction
review}. The current checker reconstructs its ten-by-ten Gram and
inverse without project arithmetic, verifies all three positive affine
kernels, and recounts the triangle incidences.

At each cusp, the link is Delta\^{}8, with seven finite-ended and two
ideal-ended ports. Thus T\_1(v)=21, T\_2(v)=14, and

\[
 T_1(v)+T_2(v)=35=5a_v.
\]

Globally T\_1=63, T\_2=21 and E\_fi=21, so T\_1+2T\_2=105=5E\_fi. This
supplies actual sharpness, not only an abstract port distribution.

The
\href{fresh_finite_vertex_t2_port_counterexample_20261017.md}{finite-vertex
T2 counterexample} does not contradict the proof. Its two triangles
share the finite--ideal edge A--Iinf, and Iinf has the square link
Delta\^{}1 x Delta\^{}1. At Iinf, the two triangular link edges \{A,I1\}
and \{A,I2\} belong to different factor fibers. They never enter one
application of the simple-at-cusp completion argument. The checker
reconstructs these fibers from the saved full edge/face incidences and
verifies (1) at all three cusps. We have not restored triangle-port
transitivity at the finite vertex A.

\section{Exact residual budget and
limits}\label{exact-residual-budget-and-limits}

Combine (1) with the sharp finite-edge inequality and the original-face
budget from the
\href{fresh_finite_volume_simplex_truncation_20261017.md}{finite-volume
report}. With its notation b\_n, alpha\_n, v\_f and E(L\_v), one obtains

\[
 \boxed{\begin{aligned}
 2T_3+Q\ \ge\ &(b_n-14n/3)v_f
       +\sum_v a_v\bigl(14/3-R_5(v)\bigr)\\
       &+\alpha_n\sum_v E(L_v)+T_1.
 \end{aligned}}                                                   \tag{4}
\]

Indeed the previous lower demand on 2(T\_2+T\_3)+Q loses at most sum\_v
a\_v R\_5(v)−T\_1 when the T\_2 contribution is subtracted. This is a
new necessary tradeoff, not an upper payment bound for T\_3 or Q. It is
vacant for the all-ideal problem in the sense that a\_v=T\_1=T\_2=0
there; the remaining all-ideal triangles and quadrilaterals still need
control. For simple cusps R\_5(v)\textless=5, while multiple small
factors can make R\_5(v) as large as n−1. No multiplicity-free
generalization of (2) is claimed.

The two primary geometric sources above were opened on2026-10-17. The
one-factor completion argument received an independent conceptual check
from construction\_audit. The parent independently read the full proof
and source, including factor-face construction, finite-port
disjointness, ideal-count scope, sharpness and residual algebra, and
found no gap. Neither read is described as a second arithmetic
implementation.

\textbf{FINAL/FROZEN.} Generation and a fresh saved-data replay pass.
Syntax, all18 direct source hashes, eight local report links and the two
primary source links were checked. This is an internally reviewed
incidence lemma with exact counting and inherited geometric sharpness,
not an ambient dimension improvement or external refereeing.
