\chapter{A subunit residual-cost envelope: dimension-164
candidate}\label{a-subunit-residual-cost-envelope-dimension-164-candidate}

\textbf{Research proof candidate, pending independent review:} the
reviewed \href{fresh_nikulin_height_charge_20261015.md}{dimension-165
argument} sharpens to dimension at most \textbf{164}. The new point is
that two large E8 defects leave less than one unit of cost for every
other factor together. That residual budget allows only one retained
contact, whose total energy loss is at most \(2/3\). This improves the
aggregate loss from \(40/9\) to \(38/9\). There is no new uniform
unit-charge claim.

The \href{../scripts/fresh_nikulin_defect_frontier_20261015.py}{exact
checker} and
\href{fresh_nikulin_defect_frontier_20261015.json}{certificate} bind the
frozen 165 source and its
\href{fresh_nikulin_height_charge_20261015_review.md}{independent
review}. They use the latter's standalone rational grounded-matrix
helper read-only. The new thresholds, complete low-cost singleton lists,
classical tail inequalities, and aggregate cases are recomputed. No
earlier artifact is modified. This package makes no
publication-priority, current-best, or formal verification claim.

\section{Unchanged local framework, with a larger height
window}\label{unchanged-local-framework-with-a-larger-height-window}

Use the same preset omissions, contact normalization, and geometric
hypotheses as the reviewed 165 proof. For each affine factor of rank r,
put \[
T=2r/9\quad\text{or}\quad2(r-1)/9
\] in the unique factor avoiding the narrow-facet node. The energy is
\(W=\min(\sigma,\tau)^2E\), and C is the sum of the two retained-support
quadratic costs. The ratio \(M=\max(\sigma/\tau,\tau/\sigma)\) is common
across all factors. Each endpoint's total cost is at most 2, hence
\(\sum C\le4\).

The 165 exceptional support lists and small-cycle convex domains are
independent of the height-window endpoint. Re-evaluating all 71
singleton energy bounds, the inexpensive two-row E7 case, and all 580
certified small-cycle convex minima at \[
\boxed{M\le B=21/20}
\] still proves the same unit-charge classification. The A large-rank
and B/C/D proofs did not use height balance and remain unchanged. Thus
every factor has \(W+C\ge T\), except possibly the same 15 E7/E8 support
occurrences:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2000}}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2667}}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2667}}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2667}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Type of actual failing factor
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedleft
Target
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedleft
Minimum cost
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedleft
Defect upper bound
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Ordinary E8 & \(16/9\) & \(14/9\) & \(2/9\) \\
Ordinary E7 or avoid-node E8 & \(14/9\) & \(3/2\) & \(1/18\) \\
\end{longtable}
}

An actual failing factor means \(T-W-C>0\). The table describes
necessary conditions, not an assertion that all listed support
possibilities attain the stated defects. At most two failing factors are
possible because three would consume at least \(9/2>4\) cost.

\section{The residual-product lemma}\label{the-residual-product-lemma}

Under \(M\le21/20\), consider any collection of the prescribed affine
factors with total retained cost \textbf{strictly less than 1}. Then \[
\boxed{\sum (T-W)\le2/3.} \tag{1}
\] This includes ordinary and avoid-node factors of every rank.

First, for any positive definite retained Gram with root squares 2, its
inverse diagonal is \[
J_{kk}=\frac1{2-v^TB^{-1}v}\ge\frac12.
\] Its inverse is entrywise nonnegative. Every nonzero contact is at
least 1, so two retained coordinates, anywhere among the two rows of all
the factors, already cost at least 1. The strict residual budget
therefore allows \textbf{at most one retained coordinate globally}. A
zero-cost factor has both rows supported at their omitted nodes and
satisfies the reviewed point-energy bound \(W\ge T\). It remains to
bound the loss of a single-contact factor.

\subsection{Exceptional factors}\label{exceptional-factors}

The checker reconstructs every retained inverse diagonal below 1 in all
40 ordinary/forbidden-node records. If \(T\le2/3\), inequality (1) for
that factor follows from \(W\ge0\). Otherwise the complete singleton
energy/height calculation gives the stronger \(W\ge T\) at \(B=21/20\).
Ordinary F4, whose target is \(8/9\), has no retained diagonal below 1.
There is no hidden multi-contact case because the total cost is strictly
below 1.

\subsection{All A cycles}\label{all-a-cycles}

For affine \(A_r\), set \(m=r+1\), choose omissions 0 and
\(h=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\), and write \(R(d)=d(m-d)/m\). A retained node
at distance d has inverse diagonal \(R(d)\). Diagonal below 1 forces
\(d=1\): for \(m\ge4\), every \(2\le d\le m/2\) has
\(R(d)\ge2(m-2)/m\ge1\); m=2,3 already have only distance 1.

Write the single-contact row as \(p=a e_i+b e_k\), where k is a neighbor
of i, \(b\ge1\), and \(a=0\) or \(a\ge1\). The other row is supported at
its omitted node j.

If a=0, both heights are at least 1, and the worst neighbor is the one
toward the opposite omission. Hence \[
W\ge R(h-1)=
\begin{cases}
m/4-1/m,&m\text{ even},\\
(m^2-9)/(4m),&m\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\] Subtracting the ordinary target \(2(m-1)/9\) and adding \(4/9\) gives
\[
\frac{m^2+24m-36}{36m},\qquad
\frac{m^2+24m-81}{36m},
\] respectively. These are nonnegative for all even m≥2 and odd m≥3, as
verified by their exact nonnegative-coefficient substitutions. Thus the
loss is at most \(4/9\), already smaller than the required \(2/3\).

If a≥1, one height is at least 2, so the smaller height is at least
\(2/B\). For m=2,3 the target is at most \(4/9\), so there is nothing
further to prove. For m≥4 the normalized-row energy is the squared
distance from a point on the segment between the two adjacent point
potentials to the other omission's potential. Its minimum, using the
worse of the two adjacent directions, is \[
E_{\min}=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{m(m-2)}{4(m-1)},&m\text{ even},\\[3pt]
\dfrac{(m+1)(m-3)}{4(m-1)},&m\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\] These follow by minimizing the exact convex quadratic
\(R(h)-\ell u+R(1)u^2\), with \(\ell=(m+\varepsilon)/m\) and
\(\varepsilon=m\bmod2\). Both minima are at least \((m-3)/4\). Therefore
\[
W-T\ge\frac{m-3}{B^2}-\frac{2(m-1)}9
=\frac{302m-1102}{441}>0\qquad(m\ge4).
\] Rotation proves the same ordinary estimate while avoiding a
prescribed node when m≥3. The coincident-omission avoid-A1 case has
target zero. This covers every A rank and every permitted omission case.

\subsection{All B/C/D ranks}\label{all-bcd-ranks}

The complete 24 prefix-coordinate classes are recomputed from the frozen
independent coordinate realization. Imposing inverse diagonal below 1
leaves only the following possibilities:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lrl@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}

\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Ordinary B, right omission, node 0 or 1 & \(r/4\) & r≤3, so T≤2/3 \\
Modified B, omission r−1, node 0 or 1 & \((r-1)/4\) & r≤4, so T≤2/3 \\
Modified B, omission r−1, node r & 1/2 & linear energy loss 0 \\
Separate modified B2 & at least 1/2 & T=2/9 \\
Modified C, omission 1, node 0 & 1/2 & linear energy loss 0 \\
Modified C, omission 1, node r & \((r-1)/2\) & r=2, so T=2/9 \\
\end{longtable}
}

All other classes have diagonal at least 1. In each zero-linear-loss
case the nonnegative quadratic-remainder identity gives \(E\ge R_{ij}\),
and both heights are at least 1, so \(W\ge R_{ij}\ge T\). In the
small-target cases, \(W\ge0\) suffices. All modified choices are
included via the previously reviewed fork/path symmetries and the
explicit modified B/C classes.

The constant \(2/3\) in (1) is sharp for this local domain. In ordinary
affine B3 with omissions (0,3), put both contact rows at node 0 with
coefficient 1. Their normalized potentials agree, giving \(M=1\),
\(E=W=0\), while the sole retained cost is \(3/4<1\) and T=2/3. Its
literal rationally scaled Gram and inverse diagonal are checked exactly.
This is a local witness, not an assertion that an arbitrary product of
extremal factors is realized by an ambient polytope.

\section{Complete defect accounting}\label{complete-defect-accounting}

Let the total loss be \(L=\sum(T-W)\). If at most one factor fails unit
charge, then \[
L\le\sum C+2/9\le38/9.
\] If two fail, classify them by the number of ordinary E8 factors:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 8\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2000}}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 8\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2000}}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 8\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2000}}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 8\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2000}}
  >{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 8\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2000}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}

Ordinary E8 among the two
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedleft
Minimum combined cost

0 & 3 & ≤1 & 28/9 & \(28/9+1=37/9\) \\
1 & 55/18 & ≤17/18 & 30/9 & \(30/9+2/3=4\) \\
2 & 28/9 & ≤8/9 & 32/9 & \(32/9+2/3=38/9\) \\
\end{longtable}
}

The first row uses unit charge for all remaining factors, which do not
fail by definition. The other two use the strict-subunit
residual-product lemma; the individual failing factors themselves are
bounded only by \(W\ge0\). This proves the full envelope \[
\boxed{L\le38/9\quad\text{whenever }M\le21/20.} \tag{2}
\] It accounts for actual costs, not just a count of possible
exceptional support records.

\section{Dimension conclusion and
scope}\label{dimension-conclusion-and-scope}

With \(N=n-1\), the sum of targets is \((2N-2)/9\), including the sole
avoid-node penalty. Equation (2) gives \[
\sum W\ge\frac{2N-40}{9},\qquad
-(x,y)\ge M\frac{N-38}{9}\quad(M\le21/20).
\] For \(M\ge21/20\), the unchanged four-thirds estimate with the same
preset omissions gives \(-(x,y)\ge M(N-43)/9\). At \(N=164+t\), these
are at least \[
14+t/9,\qquad
14+7/60+7t/60,
\] respectively. Both contradict the strict Nikulin narrow-facet pairing
bound \(-(x,y)<14\). Thus the ideal-vertex branch excludes n≥165; the
inherited compact-facet branch gives n≤143. Their combination is the
candidate \(\boxed{n\le164}\).

All geometric coverage---finite-sided finite volume, the narrow facet,
compact/ideal alternative, actual framing and terminating walls, common
height ratio, and endpoint Schur budgets---is inherited explicitly from
the reviewed 165/169/166 chain. The new result is the widened local
check and the complete strict-subunit residual envelope. No arithmetic
restriction or finite-label cutoff is imposed.

For later work, a rank-residue argument alone does not rule out the
relaxed extremal combination: two E8 factors, one B3, one avoid-A1 and
24 zero-cost ordinary E6 factors have total affine rank 164. Their
individual endpoint cost budgets may obstruct this combination, which is
stronger information than the summed cost used here. That is a separate
future question, not part of this proof or an achieved bound below 164.

Nikulin's narrow-facet theorem gives a facet F whose framing hyperplanes

cannot have negative pairing at least 14.
\href{https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf}{Official
ICM report, printed p.655}.

If F has an ideal vertex, its horospherical link is a product of

endpoints, finite volume supplies terminating walls x,y. At an ideal
endpoint, one chooses a missing node in the appropriate affine
component, or an orthogonal component if F belongs to an A1 factor. The
frozen product proof verifies that these walls meet F along actual
ridges.

For affine factor a, let C\_a be the sum of the two retained-support

give, respectively,

\begin{verbatim}
σ_a τ_a E_a / M + 2C_a ≥ 2r_a/9,
σ_a τ_a E_a / M + 2C_a ≥ 2(r_a−1)/9.
\end{verbatim}

Only the single factor containing F's normal uses the second inequality.
It holds for every forbidden node, with choices made before the contact

retained-contact cases; it imposes no label cutoff.

\chapter{Reviewed research proof candidate: dimension at most
189}\label{reviewed-research-proof-candidate-dimension-at-most-189}

\textbf{Candidate theorem.} Every finite-sided finite-volume real
hyperbolic Coxeter polytope in H\^{}n satisfies \textbf{n≤189}. There is
no arithmeticity assumption, no simple-ideal-vertex restriction, and no
facet-count or finite-label cutoff.

This package combines the frozen
\href{fresh_nikulin_dimension_225_candidate_20261015.md}{225 baseline},
the new \href{fresh_nikulin_energy_charge_20261015.md}{contact-cost
estimate}, and its
\href{fresh_nikulin_energy_charge_20261015_review.md}{independent proof
and arithmetic review}. It preserves every earlier artifact. The
\href{../scripts/fresh_nikulin_dimension_189_candidate_20261015.py}{binder}
and
\href{fresh_nikulin_dimension_189_candidate_20261015.json}{certificate}
record their source, data, and report hashes and validate the recursive
dependency manifests.

The conclusion is presented as a reviewed research proof candidate, not
as an externally peer-reviewed theorem, a publication-priority
assertion, or a determination of the current strongest known bound.
Nikulin's ICM report already announces the unrestricted inequality
n\textless300. That historical claim remains distinct from the explicit
estimates reconstructed here.
\href{https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf}{Primary
report, printed pp.657--659}.

\section{Exhaustive case split}\label{exhaustive-case-split}

Nikulin's narrow-facet theorem supplies a facet F whose framing
hyperplanes have pairwise distance strictly below arccosh 7. For outward
normals of square two, the selected framing walls x,y therefore cannot
satisfy −(x,y)≥14. The construction uses walls sharing actual ridges
with F, so they belong to the precise framing set in the theorem.
\href{https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf}{Theorem
A, printed p.655}.

If F contains an ideal vertex, its horospherical link is a product of
affine Coxeter simplices with total rank N=n−1. The frozen product
argument selects two outgoing edges, and terminating walls x,y that meet
F in actual ridges. Their normalized affine null-height ratio q is
common across all factors. With M=max(q,1/q)≥1, their Lorentz pairing is

\begin{verbatim}
−(x,y) = (1/2) Σ_a σ_a τ_a E_a − q − 1/q.
\end{verbatim}

At each terminating endpoint the total retained Schur cost is at most
two. If C\_a is the sum of the two endpoint costs in factor a, then Σ\_a
C\_a≤4. The new estimate proves

\begin{verbatim}
σ_a τ_a E_a / M ≥ 2r_a/9 − 2C_a
\end{verbatim}

for every factor except the one containing F's normal. That one factor
retains the previous uniform loss allowance of two. Consequently

\begin{verbatim}
Σ_a σ_a τ_a E_a ≥ M(2N/9−10),
−(x,y) ≥ M(N/9−7).
\end{verbatim}

For n≥190, N≥189 and the final lower bound is at least 14, contradicting
narrowness. This branch therefore gives n≤189.

If F has no ideal vertex, finite-sidedness and finite volume make F
compact: its vertices are among the finitely many finite and ideal
vertices of the ambient projective polytope. The already reviewed
\href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015_compact_facet.md}{compact-facet
lemma} gives n≤143. It uses ambient vertex diagrams and quasi-Lannér
extraction; it does not assume that F is itself a Coxeter polytope or
that its ambient face stars have no parabolic subdiagrams.

These cases exhaust the chosen narrow facet. Thus n≤max(189,143)=189.

\section{What the sharper estimate
adds}\label{what-the-sharper-estimate-adds}

The 225 proof charged a fixed loss to each of at most eight spoiled
non-narrow affine factors. The new proof charges their loss to the
actual total Schur cost, bounded by four independently of how many
factors occur.

For classical factors and affine A\_1,E\_6,F\_4,G\_2, the cost of one
retained nonright contact, together with the inherited localization
estimate, directly pays the required loss. The two exceptional issues
are E\_7 and E\_8, whose chosen deletions can leave an inexpensive A\_1
contact. Exact inverse-diagonal checks show that cost below one permits
only a single such contact. Three exact resistance values, 1/2,1,1/2,
then give the interpolation identity E=(1+u²)/2. Splitting according to
whether the omitted-node contact is zero or at least one proves the same
charge inequality. This is an all-label argument, not a search with a
maximum Coxeter label.

The independent review reconstructs the exceptional arithmetic and
checks the geometric and inequality cases. The earlier independent
reviews continue to cover common null-height scaling, the actual-ridge
endpoint selection, the prescribed omission choices, and the
compact-facet branch. The primary energy-charge report's final
pending-review sentence is historical: that report was frozen before the
separate review finished; its completed review is bound in this package.

The binder checks source closure, the exhaustive case combination, and
the exact scalar threshold. It imports no producer arithmetic. Published
classifications and the geometric proof arguments remain explicitly
identified mathematical inputs; these computational checks are not a
formal proof-assistant development.

\chapter{A research proof candidate for the finite-volume bound
225}\label{a-research-proof-candidate-for-the-finite-volume-bound-225}

\textbf{Candidate theorem.} Every finite-sided finite-volume real
hyperbolic Coxeter polytope in H\^{}n satisfies \textbf{n≤225}. No
arithmeticity, compactness, simple-ideal-vertex, facet-count, or
prescribed-diagram hypothesis is imposed.

This is a research proof candidate assembled from two explicit arguments
and their internal independent checks. It is not a claim of publication
priority, an externally peer-reviewed result, or the strongest currently
known bound. Nikulin's 1986 ICM report already announces the
unrestricted inequality n\textless300; the present work reconstructs
explicit constants rather than treating 995 as the only historical
assertion.

The
\href{../scripts/fresh_nikulin_dimension_225_candidate_20261015.py}{dependency
checker} and
\href{fresh_nikulin_dimension_225_candidate_20261015.json}{certificate}
bind the exact source, data, and proof reports. They verify the case
partition and scalar comparisons, and recursively validate the saved
source manifests. They do not purport to turn the geometric arguments or
the cited classifications into a formal proof-assistant development.

\section{The two cases}\label{the-two-cases}

Choose a narrow facet F supplied by Nikulin's narrow-facet theorem.
Hyperplanes of any two framing facets whose hyperplanes meet H(F) have
distance strictly less than arccosh 7. The proof below uses framing
facets sharing actual ridges with F, a subset of that published framing
set. With outward normals normalized to square two, such framing normals
x,y cannot satisfy −(x,y)≥14.
\href{https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf}{Nikulin,
printed p.655, Theorem A}.

\textbf{If F has an ideal vertex, use the product-cusp argument.} Its
horospherical link is a product of irreducible affine Coxeter simplices
with total rank N=n−1. Select two outgoing edges by deleting one node in
each affine component, avoiding the node of F. The terminating walls can
be chosen to meet F in actual ridges, including when the second
endpoints are ideal and nonsimple.

At either endpoint the positive-semidefinite Schur bound is at most two.
Inverse diagonals are at least one half, inverse entries are
nonnegative, and every nonright norm-two Coxeter contact has magnitude
at least one. Thus at most four retained contacts occur per endpoint. At
most eight affine factors are affected; allowing one additional factor
for the avoided narrow-facet node gives at most nine marked factors.

The \href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015_products.md}{full product proof}
proves a uniform affine energy bound 2r/9 per factor of rank r, with
loss at most two per marked factor. The two null-height ratios agree
across all affine factors, without any arithmetic or equal-scale
assumption. If M is the larger of this ratio and its reciprocal, then
M≥1 and the exact Lorentz identity yields

\begin{verbatim}
−(x,y) ≥ M ((n−1)/9 − 11).
\end{verbatim}

For n≥226 the right side is at least 14, contradicting narrowness. Hence
this case has n≤225. The
\href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015.md}{classical formulas},
\href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015_products.json}{product arithmetic},
and \href{fresh_nikulin_product_independent_20261015.md}{separate
independent arithmetic review} make the all-rank and exceptional
constants explicit.

\textbf{If F has no ideal vertex, it is compact.} This uses
finite-sidedness and finite volume: the projective closure of the
polytope is the convex hull of finitely many finite and ideal vertices,
and the vertices of a facet are among these. A facet with only finite
vertices is therefore compact. It is simple because its vertices are
finite vertices of an acute Coxeter chamber. It need not be a Coxeter
polytope itself.

Apply the separate
\href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015_compact_facet.md}{compact-facet
lemma}, which gives n≤143. Its weights are defined using the ambient
spherical vertex diagrams. Minimal indefinite subdiagrams are allowed to
be quasi-Lannér, of order at most ten. Compact triangles supply two
positive-weight corners; compact quadrilaterals supply one by a white
path of length at most 17. At each ambient finite vertex, at most 17n
pairs have that graph distance. The simple-polytope h-vector inequality
on the facet contradicts n≥144.

Thus the two exhaustive cases give n≤max(225,143)=225.

\section{What was repaired during the
audit}\label{what-was-repaired-during-the-audit}

The first proposed treatment of the compact-facet case attempted to
transfer Vinberg's finer compact-chamber weights directly. That would
have used a false intermediate assertion: a compact marked face need not
have an ambient star free of parabolic subdiagrams. A Coxeter
tetrahedron with path labels 3--3--6 supplies an explicit
counterexample.

The final compact-facet proof does not use that assertion. For a compact
quadrilateral, the full block consisting of its white support and an
opposite pair of black nodes is indefinite: a positive-definite block
would give an actual intersection of opposite sides, while a singular
positive-semidefinite block would give an ideal point on the compact
quadrilateral. Minimal-indefinite extraction then permits quasi-Lannér
diagrams. The original primary sources state the needed order-ten
classification and extraction, and the proof separately explains why
disconnected affine degeneracies cause no exception.
\href{https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&paperid=1484&what=fullteng}{Prokhorov,
§2, printed pp.407--408}.

The older frozen product report describes its result as conditional
because its all-finite alternative was unresolved at that checkpoint.
That report remains unchanged. The separate compact-facet proof supplies
the missing branch here; it does not retroactively import an unproved
compact-facet Coxeter property.

\section{Evidence and literature
status}\label{evidence-and-literature-status}

The product review reconstructs the exceptional affine matrices and
their energy constants with separate arithmetic, checks independent
classical coordinate/localization examples, and verifies the all-rank
scalar inequalities. The separate
\href{fresh_dimension225_hostile_20261015.md}{hostile mathematical
review} checks common null-height scaling, the contact budget,
predetermined omission choices, and the actual-ridge endpoint bridge. It
also audits the compact-facet source and geometry, with independent
scalar replay. The combined certificate records the specific review
files and their hashes.

The primary literature inputs are the narrow-facet theorem, spherical
and affine Coxeter classification, quasi-Lannér order at most ten, the
spherical graph-distance pair bound, and the simple-polytope h-vector
relations. The new geometric reductions and estimates are written out in
the bound reports; the checker does not silently substitute a finite
numerical search for any all-rank statement.

Nikulin's printed pp.657--659 outline the narrow-facet method, work out
an affine-A example, and announce n\textless300. The
\href{dimension_bound_prokhorov_20261015_proof_review.md}{earlier
literature audit} distinguishes that announcement from the fully
explicit 995 proof and its independently audited 990 refinement. This
combined candidate is presented for further mathematical scrutiny with
that historical distinction preserved. No current-best or novelty
assertion is made.

identities exactly, and check the all-rank inequalities below. They bind
the earlier geometric proofs rather than importing producer arithmetic.
Independent review is separate from this primary package.

\section{Setup retained from the 225
proof}\label{setup-retained-from-the-225-proof}

Choose a narrow facet F. If it is compact, the frozen
\href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015_compact_facet.md}{compact-facet
lemma} gives n≤143. Otherwise F contains an ideal vertex. Its link is a
product of affine Coxeter simplices, of ranks r\_a summing to N=n−1.

Use exactly the fixed omission choices from the
\href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015_products.md}{product-cusp proof}:
opposite cycle nodes for A, the designated end nodes for B/C/D, and the
recorded pairs for the exceptional types. Only the component containing
F's normal uses the old avoid-node modification. These choices precede
the selection of terminating contact rows.

Write x,y for the resulting two norm-two terminating walls, chosen to
share actual ridges with F. In a component let p,q be their nonnegative
negated contact rows, δ its positive affine kernel, and σ=δ·p, τ=δ·q.
The ratio σ/τ is common to all components. Put M=max(σ/τ,τ/σ)≥1. Let
E\_a be the corresponding normalized-row energy in the Euclidean cusp
quotient. The exact identity is

\begin{verbatim}
−(x,y) = (1/2) Σ_a σ_a τ_a E_a − σ_a/τ_a − τ_a/σ_a.
\end{verbatim}

For the two deletion supports S\_i,S\_j in this component define its
\textbf{contact cost}

\begin{verbatim}
C_a = p_Siᵀ G(S_i)⁻¹ p_Si + q_Sjᵀ G(S_j)⁻¹ q_Sj.
\end{verbatim}

Each endpoint's total Schur cost is at most two, so Σ\_a C\_a≤4. The
inverses are entrywise nonnegative. Every nonzero contact is at least
one, including contacts with an omitted node; no upper bound on its
label or magnitude is used.

We prove, for every component other than the one containing F's normal,

\begin{verbatim}
σ_a τ_a E_a / M ≥ 2r_a/9 − 2 C_a.                 (1)
\end{verbatim}

If C\_a=0, both rows are supported only on their omitted nodes. The
frozen point-contact bound already gives σ\_aτ\_aE\_a/M≥2r\_a/9. It
remains to consider C\_a\textgreater0.

\section{Classical and direct exceptional
factors}\label{classical-and-direct-exceptional-factors}

A positive contact in a retained row costs at least the corresponding
inverse diagonal, because its magnitude is at least one and all cross
terms are nonnegative. Thus C\_a is at least the smallest inverse
diagonal among the two retained supports.

For affine A\_r, r≥2, this minimum is r/(r+1). For r≤8, nonnegativity of
energy bounds the deficit by 2r/9, and

\begin{verbatim}
2r/(r+1) − 2r/9 = 2r(8−r)/(9(r+1)) ≥ 0.
\end{verbatim}

For r≥9 the unchanged localization argument gives energy at least
(r−8)/4 after division by M, so the deficit is at most 2−r/36. Here

\begin{verbatim}
2r/(r+1) − (2−r/36) = (r−8)(r+9)/(36(r+1)) ≥ 0.
\end{verbatim}

Both ranges prove (1). Affine A\_1 is separate: its retained inverse
diagonal is 1/2 and its baseline is only 2/9, so the zero-energy bound
suffices.

For the unmodified B/D end deletions, the retained inverse minimum is at
least one in ranks r≥4. The B\_2 and B\_3 presentations have minimum
respectively 1/2 and 3/4; their zero-energy baseline is already smaller
than twice that value. For r≤9 the bound 2r/9≤2 suffices. For r≥10, the
old localization gives energy at least (r−5)/4 after division by M, so
the deficit is at most 5/4−r/36\textless2. This proves (1) for B and D.

For C\_r, r≥2, either end deletion leaves finite B\_r, with inverse
minimum one. The zero-energy argument covers r≤9. In larger rank the
retained bound (r−5)/2 already has deficit at most 5/2−5r/18≤2. Thus (1)
holds here as well. These claims use the closed inverse formulas in the
frozen classical proof; the checker separately verifies the low B ranks
where the generic minimum-one statement would be false.

The direct exceptional cases are also immediate from their exact inverse
diagonals:

In each row the point energy is at least 2r/9, and twice the last entry
is also at least 2r/9. Zero energy therefore suffices whenever a
retained contact occurs. The node numbering is fixed by the full
matrices in the certificate.

\section{The inexpensive E\_7 and E\_8
contacts}\label{the-inexpensive-e_7-and-e_8-contacts}

A minimum-diagonal argument alone would fail in these two types. The
fixed E\_7 omissions 3,6 each isolate an A\_1 node, respectively 4,7.
The fixed E\_8 omissions 3,7 have just one inverse diagonal below one:
node 8 after omitting 7. Each of these inexpensive diagonals is 1/2;
every other retained inverse diagonal is at least one. The checker
verifies the entire two inverse-diagonal lists, rather than only these
three selected entries.

If C\_a≥1, inequality (1) follows from nonnegative energy since
2r/9\textless2 for r=7,8. Suppose 0\textless C\_a\textless1.
Nonnegativity of inverse entries implies that there is exactly
\textbf{one} retained nonzero contact across the two endpoint rows: it
is one of the inexpensive A\_1 contacts. Two such contacts would already
cost at least one, and any other retained contact would cost at least
one by itself.

Orient the two rows so that this contact, of magnitude b≥1, belongs to
x. Let i be x's omitted node, l the inexpensive retained node, and j the
other endpoint's omitted node. The kernel is normalized so that

\begin{verbatim}
δ_i=δ_j=2,   δ_l=1.
\end{verbatim}

The contact rows consequently have the exact forms

\begin{verbatim}
p = a e_i + b e_l,       q = c e_j,
σ = 2a+b,               τ = 2c,
C_a = b²/2.
\end{verbatim}

Here c≥1 because the second row cannot vanish, and a is either zero or
at least one. This last alternative is the only discreteness used: a
nonright Coxeter contact cannot have magnitude strictly between zero and
one.

For nodes u,v let R\_uv be the squared energy of the normalized
point-row difference e\_u/δ\_u−e\_v/δ\_v. In each of the three
inexpensive-contact cases, exact inversion gives

\begin{verbatim}
R_ij=1/2,   R_lj=1,   R_il=1/2.                  (2)
\end{verbatim}

If a=0, the normalized first row is the point row at l. Hence E\_a=1.
Since both σ,τ≥1,

\begin{verbatim}
σ τ E_a/M = min(σ,τ)² E_a ≥ 1,
2C_a=b²≥1.
\end{verbatim}

Their sum is at least two, which exceeds the required baseline 2r/9.

If a≥1, both σ and τ are at least two. Put u=b/(2a+b). The first
normalized row is the convex combination (1−u)e\_i/δ\_i+u e\_l/δ\_l. The
standard squared-distance interpolation identity and (2) give

\begin{verbatim}
E_a = (1−u)R_ij+uR_lj−u(1−u)R_il
    = (1+u²)/2 ≥ 1/2.
\end{verbatim}

Therefore σ τ E\_a/M = min(σ,τ)² E\_a≥2, so (1) follows even without
adding its contact cost. The same argument applies when the inexpensive
contact belongs to y. This closes all E\_7/E\_8 possibilities, including
arbitrary large finite labels and dotted omitted contacts.

\section{Summing the costs and completing the
dichotomy}\label{summing-the-costs-and-completing-the-dichotomy}

The one component containing F's normal keeps the frozen estimate

\begin{verbatim}
σ_a τ_a E_a/M ≥ 2r_a/9 − 2.
\end{verbatim}

There is no need to charge that component's cost, or to optimize its
omission choices. Summing (1) over the other components and using Σ\_a
C\_a≤4 gives

\begin{verbatim}
Σ_a σ_a τ_a E_a ≥ M(2N/9 − 8 − 2).
\end{verbatim}

Since σ\_a/τ\_a+τ\_a/σ\_a≤2M, the Lorentz identity implies

\begin{verbatim}
−(x,y) ≥ M(N/9−7).
\end{verbatim}

For n≥190, N=n−1≥189 and the right side is at least 14. Both x,y are
actual framing walls of the narrow facet, so this contradicts its strict
distance bound arccosh 7. Thus the ideal-vertex branch now gives n≤189.

If the chosen narrow facet has only finite vertices, finite-sidedness
and finite volume make it compact, and the unchanged compact-facet proof
gives n≤143. The two cases therefore yield the stated candidate bound
n≤189.

This argument changes the energy accounting only. It does not change the
225 baseline artifacts, the endpoint-existence argument, cusp rank
decomposition, positive common null-height ratio, or the proof that the
selected ending walls meet the exact narrow-facet framing condition. Its
classification and primary-source scope are those documented in the
frozen \href{fresh_nikulin_dimension_225_candidate_20261015.md}{combined
candidate and audit}. Independent scrutiny of the new contact-cost step
is required before using this sharper value as a checked checkpoint.

\chapter{Independent hostile review of the contact-cost
bound}\label{independent-hostile-review-of-the-contact-cost-bound}

\textbf{PASS.} No gap was found in the new charging argument giving the
research candidate \textbf{n≤189} for finite-sided finite-volume real
hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes, using the explicitly inherited geometric
and published inputs. The review makes no publication-priority or
current-best claim. The previously frozen 225 proof and review are
unchanged.

This note reviews \href{fresh_nikulin_energy_charge_20261015.md}{the new
argument}. Its
\href{../scripts/fresh_nikulin_energy_charge_20261015_review.py}{independent
checker} and
\href{fresh_nikulin_energy_charge_20261015_review.json}{saved
certificate} use only standard-library \texttt{Fraction} arithmetic.
They import no producer code or algebra engine. Exceptional energies are
calculated by grounding a coordinate in rationally congruent affine Gram
matrices, rather than using the producer's regularized inverse. All
complete physical Gram entries, retained inverse diagonals, and relevant
point energies agree.

\section{Scope of the new proof}\label{scope-of-the-new-proof}

The proposed improvement changes only the loss assigned to a non-narrow
affine factor. The prior
\href{fresh_dimension225_hostile_20261015.md}{hostile 225 audit}
supplies the finite/ideal narrow-facet dichotomy, actual-ridge
terminating-wall construction, positive common null-height ratio,
relative factor scales, and compact-facet bound n≤143. The classical
localization and fixed omission choices are inherited from their bound
primary proofs. No geometric hypothesis is silently strengthened, and
the new calculation does not re-prove these inputs through a finite
matrix census.

Let C be the sum of the two endpoint Schur costs in one factor. Their
global sum is at most four, because each norm-two endpoint contributes
at most two. Each retained inverse is entrywise nonnegative, and every
nonzero norm-two Coxeter contact has magnitude at least one. Thus a
retained contact costs at least its inverse diagonal, regardless of how
large its label or dotted product is. An omitted contact is either zero
or at least one as well; it has not been assumed finite.

The quotient energy is nonnegative. Writing M for the common maximum of
the two reciprocal null-height ratios gives the exact identity

\begin{verbatim}
sigma*tau/M = min(sigma,tau)^2.
\end{verbatim}

This identity is unchanged by a separate positive normalization of each
affine kernel. Therefore the scale conventions in the exceptional
calculations do not introduce a hidden common-scale assumption.

\section{Exceptional factors and the low-cost
cases}\label{exceptional-factors-and-the-low-cost-cases}

The independent checker reconstructs A1, E6, E7, E8, F4 and G2, with the
fixed omissions from the earlier product proof. For F4 and G2 it clears
radical edges by positive diagonal congruence and tracks the diagonal
scaling exactly. The actual inverse diagonals, rather than the diagonals
of the rescaled matrices, are compared. Positive definiteness of every
retained block and nonnegativity of every inverse entry are checked.

The direct A1/E6/F4/G2 factors satisfy both needed inequalities: the
zero-contact point energy is at least 2r/9, and twice the minimum
retained inverse diagonal is at least 2r/9. Nonnegative energy then
handles every positive cost. The low B2 and B3 presentations are
independently reconstructed; their minimum retained inverse diagonals
are 1/2 and 3/4, respectively. They are not incorrectly assigned the
generic lower bound one.

For E7 and E8, costs at least one are harmless because 2r/9\textless2.
If 0\textless C\textless1, the complete inverse lists leave precisely
one nonzero retained contact across both rows. It is an isolated A1
entry of inverse diagonal 1/2. Two inexpensive contacts would already
cost at least one; any other retained contact would do so alone. Thus,
after possibly exchanging endpoints, the rows really are

\begin{verbatim}
p = a*e_i + b*e_l,    q = c*e_j,
sigma = 2a+b,         tau = 2c,       C=b^2/2,
\end{verbatim}

with b,c≥1 and a either zero or at least one. The zero row is excluded
by the inherited positive null-height argument. The independent matrices
give delta\_i=delta\_j=2 and delta\_l=1 in all three cheap cases: E7 has
two, E8 one.

The grounded calculations independently yield R\_ij=1/2, R\_lj=1 and
R\_il=1/2. Hence the interpolation energy is exactly (1+u²)/2, where
u=b/(2a+b). If a=0, the energy is one and min(sigma,tau)≥1, so weighted
energy plus twice the cost is at least 1+1=2. If a≥1, min(sigma,tau)≥2
and energy≥1/2, so weighted energy alone is at least two. Both exceed
the required baseline 2r/9. The inequalities remain valid for arbitrary
allowed contact magnitudes; no angle truncation is present.

\section{Classical factors and the A9
boundary}\label{classical-factors-and-the-a9-boundary}

The all-rank charging comparisons have positive, explicit expressions.
For A\_r with 2≤r≤8 the zero-energy margin is 2r(8−r)/(9(r+1)). For
r=9+t, t≥0, the large-rank margin is

\begin{verbatim}
(t+1)(t+18) / (36(t+10)) > 0.
\end{verbatim}

The corresponding B/D and C margins at r=10+t are 37/36+t/36 and
41/18+5t/18. The inverse-minimum and energy assumptions here are exactly
those in the bound classical proof; no rank sampling is substituted for
their closed formulas.

There is one range extension requiring an explicit check: the old
product report stated its localization estimates for r≥10, while the new
A argument starts at r=9. In A9 the inverse diagonal at distance three
from an end is 21/10\textgreater2; all five middle entries exceed two.
Thus only the first two and last two retained nodes can be contacted.
Opposite deletions in the affine 10-cycle leave two intervening arcs of
length one. Their effective conductance is 1/2, which is stronger than
the needed (9−8)/4=1/4. The new boundary rank is therefore covered
directly, rather than inferred from the old stated range.

\section{Global conclusion and
limitations}\label{global-conclusion-and-limitations}

Every non-narrow factor now satisfies weighted energy divided by M at
least 2r/9−2C. Summing its cost losses gives at most eight. The one
narrow factor retains the old loss allowance two, even if it itself also
uses contact cost. This double allowance is conservative; no cost is
omitted from the global upper bound.

Consequently total energy is at least M(2N/9−10). In the Lorentz
identity the reciprocal-height term is at most 2M, giving
−(x,y)≥M(N/9−7). At n≥190, N=n−1≥189, so this is at least 14. The
inherited actual-ridge result puts both selected walls in the framing
set of the strict arccosh(7) narrow facet, contradicting that bound for
square-two normals. The compact-facet branch remains n≤143. The two
branches give n≤189 with the same generality as the earlier candidate.

This conclusion does not rely on arithmeticity, simplicity at ideal
vertices, a single affine cusp factor, a finite label bound, or a common
relative scale for distinct cusp factors. Its published-source and
geometric dependencies are explicit. This is an independent research
proof audit, not a claim of external peer review or a
literature-priority determination.

\chapter{Near-balanced unit charge with a shared defect
budget}\label{near-balanced-unit-charge-with-a-shared-defect-budget}

\textbf{Research proof candidate, pending independent review:} every
finite-sided finite-volume real hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has
dimension at most \textbf{165}. The new step counts the few factors
where unit charging can fail. Each such factor consumes at least 3/2 of
a shared budget of four, so at most two can occur. This improves the
accounting in the frozen, reviewed
\href{fresh_nikulin_coupled_charge_20261015_dimension166.md}{166
candidate}; it does not alter that package or assert a new uniform local
charge coefficient.

The \href{../scripts/fresh_nikulin_height_charge_20261015.py}{checker}
and \href{fresh_nikulin_height_charge_20261015.json}{certificate} pass
generation and saved replay. They import no producer arithmetic. This is
producer verification; independent review remains necessary. No
publication-priority, current-best, or formal-verification claim is
made.

\section{Local variables and the aggregate
statement}\label{local-variables-and-the-aggregate-statement}

Use exactly the preset omissions and geometric hypotheses of the
\href{fresh_nikulin_unit_charge_20261015_review.md}{reviewed four-thirds
proof} and
\href{fresh_nikulin_coupled_charge_20261015_review.md}{common-height
proof}. An affine factor has rank r, Gram G with root squares two,
positive kernel δ normalized by min δ=1, and omissions i,j. Its two
contact rows p,q are nonnegative and nonzero; each nonzero entry is at
least one. Each endpoint's retained-support cost, summed across all
factors, is at most two. Put

\[
\sigma=\delta\cdot p,\quad\tau=\delta\cdot q,\quad
M=\max(\sigma/\tau,\tau/\sigma),\qquad
C=p_{S_i}^{T}G(S_i)^{-1}p_{S_i}+q_{S_j}^{T}G(S_j)^{-1}q_{S_j},
\] \[
W=\min(\sigma,\tau)^2E,
\qquad T=2r/9\quad\text{or}\quad2(r-1)/9
\]

in the unique factor avoiding the narrow-facet node. The ratio M is
common to all factors. The same omission choices are used in both height
ranges below.

For \textbf{M≤31/30}, every factor has W+C≥T, with the following
controlled exception: a failing factor must be one of explicitly listed
E7/E8 support patterns, must have C≥3/2, and always satisfies

\[
W+C\ge T-2/9. \tag{1}
\]

Because the shared total cost is at most four, three failing factors are
impossible. Thus, writing N=Σr=n−1 and summing all targets,

\[
\sum W\ge\frac{2N}{9}-\frac29-4-2\frac29
=\frac{2N-42}{9}. \tag{2}
\]

This does not contradict the exact balanced E8 counterexample to unit
charge. That example is one of the expensive exceptions and remains
admissible in the local domain.

\section{The height estimate}\label{the-height-estimate}

If σ≥h and τ≥k, then the ratio bound B=31/30 gives

\[
\min(\sigma,\tau)^2\ge
H(h,k):=\max\{\min(h,k)^2,\max(h,k)^2/B^2\}. \tag{3}
\]

All arguments below permit arbitrary real contact magnitudes with the
zero-or-at-least-one gap. No finite-label cutoff is used.

\section{Complete exceptional support
coverage}\label{complete-exceptional-support-coverage}

The checker reconstructs the literal affine A1, E6, E7, E8, F4 and G2
Grams, their positive kernels, every retained inverse and all 40
ordinary/avoid-node records. These records exactly match the frozen
preset choices.

If C≥T, unit charging is immediate from W≥0. Otherwise every retained
nonzero coordinate has inverse diagonal below T. All inverse entries are
nonnegative, so setting each retained nonzero coordinate to one gives a
rigorous support-cost lower bound, including every same-row cross term.
The checker enumerates \textbf{every subset} of the cheap-coordinate
list. No support-size cutoff is imposed. Precisely 71 singleton and 16
multiple-contact occurrences survive C\textless T; none has more than
two retained coordinates.

For a singleton, orient the rows as p=a e\_i+b e\_l and q=c e\_j, with
b,c≥1 and a=0 or a≥1. Let R\_uv be the normalized point-potential
resistance and put

\[
E(u)=(1-u)R_{ij}+uR_{lj}-u(1-u)R_{il},\qquad0\le u\le1.
\]

When a=0, the lower bound is H(δ\_l,δ\_j)R\_lj+c\_il. When a≥1, it is
H(δ\_i+δ\_l,δ\_j) min E+c\_il. The convex quadratic minimum is evaluated
exactly at its endpoints and any interior stationary point. Both lower
bounds meet T in \textbf{all 71 occurrences}, proving unit charging for
every singleton.

One multiple-contact pattern is also harmless: ordinary E7 with
omissions (3,6), retained nodes 4 and 7 on the respective rows. The cost
is at least one and

\[
E(u,v)=\tfrac12(1+u^2+v^2).
\]

If both omitted coordinates vanish, u=v=1, so W+C≥5/2. If either omitted
coordinate is nonzero, one height is at least three, and (3) gives
W+C≥9/(2B²)+1. Both bounds exceed T=14/9.

The remaining 15 occurrences need no energy estimate beyond W≥0:

\section{All classical A ranks}\label{all-classical-a-ranks}

For affine A\_r set m=r+1 and choose opposite cycle nodes 0 and h=⌊m/2⌋.
The kernel entries are one. The point resistance and retained inverse
entries are

\[
R(k)=\frac{k(m-k)}m,\qquad
J^{(i)}_{kl}=\frac{R(k-i)+R(l-i)-R(k-l)}2,
\]

with arguments reduced modulo m. These are the frozen all-rank cycle
identities. An explicit Euclidean realization is
v\_k=e\_1+⋯+e\_k−(k/m)(e\_1+⋯+e\_m), with v\_0=0. Its inner products are
min(k,l)−kl/m=(R(k)+R(l)−R(k−l))/2; the checker verifies this identity
for every used point pair.

For m=2,\ldots,17 the checker lists every retained coordinate with
diagonal at most two, enumerates every subset, and retains precisely the
supports whose unit-coordinate cost is at most two. Entrywise
nonnegative inverses make this a complete necessary list for actual
endpoint rows. For each pair with total minimum cost below T, it checks
both possibilities---zero or nonzero---for each omitted coordinate.

Let U,V be the resulting full nonempty supports. The normalized endpoint
potentials lie in conv\{v\_k:k∈U\} and conv\{v\_k:k∈V\}. Their heights
are at least \textbar U\textbar{} and \textbar V\textbar. For each of
\textbf{580 cases}, the certificate supplies an exact rational
closest-pair dual witness proving E≥e. Combining it with (3) and the
complete minimum support cost gives

\[
W+C\ge H(|U|,|V|)e+C_{\min}\ge T. \tag{4}
\]

The dual witnesses are independently checkable without trusting an
optimizer. For the signed Gram H of the two point lists and the two
simplex-sum constraints A, the saved nonnegative barycentric vector x
and multipliers λ satisfy Ax=(1,1), Hx+Aᵀλ≥0, and complementary
slackness. Positive semidefiniteness of H is supplied by the explicit
Euclidean point-potential realization. These conditions prove the global
quadratic minimum. Singular minimizer sets do not cause a completeness
assumption: one checked dual witness suffices for each complete support
case. No floating-point solver is used.

For all larger cycles a single analytic inequality replaces the finite
calculation. The individual cost budget two excludes every retained node
at cyclic distance d≥3, because 3(m−3)/m\textgreater2 for m≥10 and the
inverse diagonal increases to the antipode. For d≤2, with ε=m mod 2, the
frozen linear-loss identity gives

\[
c=\frac{d(m-d)}m,\quad
\ell\le\frac{(m+\varepsilon)d}m,
\quad\frac\ell c\le\frac{m+\varepsilon}{m-2}.
\]

Since C≤4 and W≥E, it follows that

\[
W+C\ge R(h)-\frac{4(2+\varepsilon)}{m-2}. \tag{5}
\]

For even m≥18 the excess of the right side over T is

\[
\frac{m^2+6m-304}{36(m-2)}>0.
\]

For odd m≥19 it is

\[
\frac{m^3+6m^2-457m+18}{36m(m-2)}>0.
\]

Substitution m=18+2t or 19+2t yields numerators with strictly positive
constant terms and nonnegative remaining coefficients for every t≥0.
Both symbolic substitutions are checked exactly. This proves all ranks;
it is not an extrapolation from the 580 cases. Rotating the same
opposite omission pair avoids a prescribed node and proves the stronger
ordinary target whenever m≥3. The remaining affine A1 avoid-node case is
already immediate.

\section{Classical B, C and D}\label{classical-b-c-and-d-1}

Use the complete 24 prefix-coordinate classes from the independently
reviewed four-thirds proof. Re-evaluate their thresholds at
C\textless T, rather than T/(4/3). All nondistant contacts have ℓ≤c, so
the linear-loss identity directly gives unit charging. The other
contacts have cost r/4, r/2, (r−1)/4 or (r−1)/2, which exceeds T=2r/9 or
2(r−1)/9 and is impossible in this range. Every index-class substitution
is checked symbolically with independent nonnegative rank and index
parameters.

The same point resistances exceed the respective targets. Modified B2
has minimum positive retained cost 1/2\textgreater T=2/9, and zero-cost
point energy one. Thus every B/C/D rank satisfies W+C≥T without using
height balance. The proof inherits the previously reviewed completeness
of these coordinate classes; the new strict threshold comparisons are
recomputed.

\section{Global split and dimension
165}\label{global-split-and-dimension-165}

The reviewed geometric chain supplies actual framing walls for a Nikulin
narrow facet, one common M across the affine product, total cost at most
four, the unique avoid-node loss 2/9, and the strict norm-two pairing
bound −(x,y)\textless14. These are inherited hypotheses, not
consequences of the local support calculations.

In the range M≤31/30, equation (2) and the unchanged Lorentz identity
give

\[
-(x,y)\ge M\frac{N-39}{9}. \tag{6}
\]

For M≥31/30, retain the frozen four-thirds estimate with exactly the
same preset omissions:

\[
-(x,y)\ge M\frac{N-43}{9}. \tag{7}
\]

At N=165+t, t≥0, (6) is at least 14+t/9, while (7) is at least

\[
\frac{31}{30}\frac{122+t}{9}
=14+\frac1{135}+\frac{31t}{270}>14.
\]

Both contradict the strict narrow-facet bound. Therefore the
ideal-vertex branch excludes n≥166 and gives n≤165. The separately
reviewed compact-facet branch still gives n≤143. Their combination is
the stated candidate n≤165, with no arithmetic assumption and no
restriction to simple cusps.

The improvement comes from an integer count of expensive exceptional
factors. A smaller uniform local coefficient alone could not give it:
the exact balanced E8 obstruction requires at least 8/7, whose scalar
threshold still rounds to 166. The present argument neither assumes that
8/7 is a valid uniform upper coefficient nor changes any frozen omission
rule.

\chapter{Independent review of the height-charge dimension-165
candidate}\label{independent-review-of-the-height-charge-dimension-165-candidate}

\textbf{The new local estimates and their global accounting pass this
independent review.} No mathematical discrepancy was found. The
resulting research proof candidate gives dimension at most 165 for
finite-sided, finite-volume real hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes,
conditional only on the explicitly inherited geometric chain already
reviewed in the preceding packages. This is an internal mathematical and
exact-arithmetic review, not a formal verification, publication-priority
claim, or independent reproduction of all historical geometric inputs.

The \href{fresh_nikulin_height_charge_20261015.md}{primary proof},
\href{../scripts/fresh_nikulin_height_charge_20261015_review.py}{independent
checker}, and
\href{fresh_nikulin_height_charge_20261015_review.json}{review
certificate} are separate artifacts. The checker uses standalone
\texttt{Fraction} arithmetic, grounded matrix inverses, rational
convex-dual verification, and polynomial coefficient arithmetic. It
imports \textbf{no project or producer code, SymPy, optimizer, or
floating-point solver}. It binds the final primary PY/JSON, not its
report.

\section{Exceptional factors: exhaustive support
coverage}\label{exceptional-factors-exhaustive-support-coverage}

The checker independently builds the literal affine A1/E6/E7/E8/F4/G2
matrices. For the last two it uses rationally scaled root bases; the
physical norm-two Gram is checked entry by entry through signs and
squares. Grounding one node gives a rational principal inverse, from
which the positive kernel, normalized kernel squares, and point
resistances are recovered. Every principal deletion is positive
definite, and every retained inverse is entrywise nonnegative. The
ordinary and forbidden-node omission rules are reconstructed explicitly,
rather than copied from the new record list.

All 40 records agree with the frozen preset choices. The
zero-retained-contact case is checked in each record, including the
coincident-omission A1 case, whose target is zero.

Write \(T=2r/9\), or \(2(r-1)/9\) in the single forbidden-node factor.
If actual total cost \(C\ge T\), the unit-charge conclusion follows from
\(W\ge0\). Otherwise each retained nonzero coordinate has inverse
diagonal strictly below T. Because every nonzero contact is at least 1
and all inverse entries are nonnegative, replacing the contacts in a
fixed support by 1 is a valid cost lower bound, including all same-row
cross terms. The independent checker enumerates \textbf{every subset} of
that full cheap-coordinate set. There is no support-size or finite-angle
cutoff.

This reconstructs exactly 71 singleton and 16 multiple-contact
occurrences; none of the latter has more than two retained coordinates.
For each singleton, the resistance quadratic is reconstructed
independently and minimized at the endpoints and its stationary point.
With \(B=31/30\), the bound \[
\min(\sigma,\tau)^2\ge
\max\!\left\{\min(h,k)^2,\frac{\max(h,k)^2}{B^2}\right\}
\] is valid regardless of which endpoint has the larger actual height.
Separate zero/nonzero omitted-coordinate cases give the claimed unit
charge in all 71 occurrences. Multiplying a separately valid energy
lower bound by a separately valid nonnegative height lower bound is
safe; no unproved correlation is required.

The sole inexpensive multiple support is the ordinary E7 pattern with
one contact at node 4 of the first row and node 7 of the second.
Polarization of the grounded resistance data gives exactly \[
E(u,v)=\tfrac12(1+u^2+v^2),\qquad C\ge1.
\] If both omitted coordinates vanish, \(u=v=1\), so \(W+C\ge5/2\).
Otherwise one height is at least 3; the common ratio bound gives
\(W+C\ge9/(2B^2)+1\). Both exceed \(14/9\).

The other 15 occurrences have cost at least \(3/2\) and possible deficit
at most \(2/9\), just using \(W\ge0\). More precisely, the four ordinary
E7 occurrences have cost \(3/2\) and deficit at most \(1/18\); the four
ordinary E8 occurrences have cost \(14/9\) and deficit at most \(2/9\);
the seven forbidden-node E8 records have cost \(3/2\) and deficit at
most \(1/18\). The seven records represent alternative forbidden-node
choices, not seven factors simultaneously present. The review does not
assume every possible defect is attained; these are safe upper bounds on
actual failure.

\section{Small A cycles: complete domains and exact dual
certificates}\label{small-a-cycles-complete-domains-and-exact-dual-certificates}

For each cycle size \(m=2,\ldots,17\), a separately computed inverse of
the grounded A-type path reconstructs all point inner products: \[
K_{ij}=\min(i,j)-ij/m.
\] These agree with the explicit Euclidean vectors
\(v_k=e_1+\cdots+e_k-(k/m)\sum_{a=1}^m e_a\). Their squared distances
are \(R(i-j)\). Thus the signed Gram used for the two point lists is
positive semidefinite, including singular and coincident-potential
cases.

The independent checker lists all retained nodes whose individual cost
is at most 2, enumerates all their subsets, and computes every same-row
cross term. It then rebuilds both endpoint domains, all domain pairs
with total minimum cost below T, and both zero/nonzero possibilities for
each omitted coordinate. The complete list has \textbf{580 cases},
agreeing exactly with the primary. Actual contact coefficients may be
arbitrary real numbers at least 1; the support enumeration therefore
covers more than a finite label set.

For every case it verifies the saved rational barycentric vector x and
multipliers \(\lambda\): \[
x\ge0,\quad Ax=(1,1),\quad
s=Hx+A^T\lambda\ge0,\quad x_i s_i=0.
\] It also checks \(x^THx=-\sum\lambda_i\). For any other feasible z, \[
z^THz-x^THx=(z-x)^TH(z-x)+2z^Ts\ge0.
\] This independently establishes the global convex minimum; no trust in
the producer's active-set optimizer or its treatment of degenerate
minimizers is needed. One verified dual witness suffices for each
completely enumerated support case. Allowing zero barycentric
coordinates relaxes the actual positive-contact domain, which is valid
for a lower bound.

The actual heights are at least the two full support sizes. Combining
the height estimate with the verified convex energy and support-cost
lower bounds proves unit charge in every case.

\section{Unbounded classical ranks}\label{unbounded-classical-ranks}

For a large A cycle, a retained coordinate at cyclic distance at least 3
costs at least \(3(m-3)/m>2\), and is impossible under the individual
endpoint budget. The inverse diagonal increases up to the antipode, so
this excludes all larger distances, not merely distance 3. At distance
\(d\le2\), the two directions have linear losses
\(d(m\pm\varepsilon)/m\), where \(\varepsilon=m\bmod2\), while the cost
is \(d(m-d)/m\). Therefore the loss-to-cost ratio is at most
\((m+\varepsilon)/(m-2)\).

The frozen nonnegative-quadratic-remainder identity gives the energy
lower bound after these linear losses. Since both heights are at least
1, \(W\ge E\); since \(C\le4\), \[
W+C\ge R(\lfloor m/2\rfloor)-\frac{4(2+\varepsilon)}{m-2}.
\] The independent checker reconstructs the cleared excess numerators \[
m^2+6m-304\quad(m\text{ even}),\qquad
m^3+6m^2-457m+18\quad(m\text{ odd}).
\] Substitution \(m=18+2t\) or \(19+2t\) gives strictly positive
constant terms and nonnegative remaining coefficients, with positive
denominators. This proves every larger rank. It also verifies the
cross-multiplied identities with the point resistance and target,
independently of symbolic parsing. Rotation preserves the ordinary
opposite-omission estimate and avoids any prescribed node when
\(m\ge3\). The remaining A1 avoid-node case has target zero.

For B/C/D the review independently re-derives all 24 prefix-coordinate
classes using rational interval segments and affine polynomials in
nonnegative rank and node-index parameters. It verifies the point-energy
surplus, and in each class either the linear loss is at most its inverse
diagonal or that diagonal strictly exceeds T. The latter excludes the
contact in the relevant range \(C<T\). Modified B2 is checked separately
by an exact grounded matrix. The geometric realization, complete class
partition, and omission symmetries are the same explicitly inherited
ones as in the
\href{fresh_nikulin_unit_charge_20261015_review.md}{independently
reviewed four-thirds proof}. No new rank cutoff or omitted classical
family is introduced here.

\section{Shared budget and common-height
split}\label{shared-budget-and-common-height-split}

Define an actual failing factor by \(T-W-C>0\). The complete local
analysis shows that it consumes actual cost at least \(3/2\), and loses
at most \(2/9\). Since the two endpoint budgets give \(\sum C\le4\),
three failing factors would cost at least \(9/2>4\). Thus at most two
factors can fail. This counts factors, not the number of candidate
support records.

With \(N=n-1=\sum r\) and the single avoid-node target penalty \(2/9\),
\[
\sum W\ge\frac{2N}{9}-\frac29-4-\frac49
=\frac{2N-42}{9}.
\] The unchanged Lorentz identity consequently gives
\(-(x,y)\ge M(N-39)/9\) for \(1\le M\le31/30\). In the other range the
reviewed four-thirds estimate, with the \textbf{same preset omissions},
gives \(-(x,y)\ge M(N-43)/9\). At \(N=165+t\), the respective lower
bounds are at least \[
14+t/9,\qquad
14+1/135+31t/270.
\] Both contradict the strict narrow-facet pairing bound \(-(x,y)<14\).
The equality endpoint of the near range is handled by that strict bound.
The ideal-vertex branch therefore gives \(n\le165\); the inherited
compact facet branch gives \(n\le143\).

This step genuinely uses the shared cost budget and common height ratio.
It does not assert a uniform unit-charge lemma, which is false, or
assume that the balanced counterexamples disappear. The same omission
choices in both ranges avoid any circular dependence on the subsequently
found walls.

\section{Dependencies and final
status}\label{dependencies-and-final-status}

The new checker and this review establish the changed local
inequalities, complete support coverage, exact dual certificates,
all-rank algebra, and global numerical accounting. The following remain
explicit previously reviewed geometric inputs: Nikulin's narrow facet
and its strict constant; the compact/ideal facet dichotomy; actual
terminating walls and framing ridges; nonzero contact rows with the
Coxeter gap; a common height ratio across all affine factors; the two
endpoint Schur budgets; and the compact-facet 143 branch. They are bound
through the frozen
\href{fresh_nikulin_unit_charge_20261015_dimension169.md}{169} and
\href{fresh_nikulin_coupled_charge_20261015_dimension166.md}{166}
chains. The present review does not silently replace those geometric
premises by a finite computation.

Independent generation and saved replay pass. Source hashes, syntax, and
local links pass. No primary changes were requested.

\chapter{Explicit separation at classical irreducible cusps of a narrow
facet}\label{explicit-separation-at-classical-irreducible-cusps-of-a-narrow-facet}

\textbf{Conditional geometric bounds, with all rank parameters
explicit.} Let
(P\ensuremath{\subset}\texttt{\textbackslash{}mathbb\ }H\^{}n) be a
finite-sided finite-volume Coxeter polytope. Suppose a Nikulin narrow
facet (F) contains an ideal vertex whose \textbf{full} cusp diagram is
one irreducible affine classical diagram. Then the following bounds
hold:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lr@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Full cusp diagram & Bound on ambient dimension (n) \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
(\texttt{\textbackslash{}widetilde\ }A\_\{n-1\}) &
(n\ensuremath{\le135}) \\
(\texttt{\textbackslash{}widetilde\ }B\_\{n-1\}) &
(n\ensuremath{\le51}) \\
(\texttt{\textbackslash{}widetilde\ }C\_\{n-1\}) &
(n\ensuremath{\le47}) \\
(\texttt{\textbackslash{}widetilde\ }D\_\{n-1\}) &
(n\ensuremath{\le55}) \\
\end{longtable}
}

The proof supplies explicit parts of the missing narrow-facet argument.
It does \textbf{not} prove a new unrestricted dimension bound, the full
historical assertion (n\textless300), or a bound for every simple
finite-volume polytope. Products of affine components and a chosen
narrow facet having only finite vertices remain untreated. No novelty or
strongest-known-bound claim is made.

The \href{../scripts/fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015.py}{exact checker}
and \href{fresh_nikulin_narrow_20261015.json}{certificate} verify closed
inverse formulas, Lorentz-coordinate identities, energy inequalities and
the boundary indexing with \texttt{Fraction} arithmetic. The proofs
below, rather than a finite rank cutoff, establish the all-rank
statements.

\section{Published input and geometric
conventions}\label{published-input-and-geometric-conventions}

\href{https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf}{Nikulin's
ICM report}, printed p.655, gives a facet (F) such that the hyperplanes
of any two facets whose hyperplanes meet (H(F)) have distance less than
(\ensuremath{\operatorname{arccosh}}7). Printed pp.657--659 describe
terminating walls on cusp edges and illustrate affine (A), obtaining
(n\textless140). We use the narrow-facet theorem and reconstruct the
separation calculation independently. The
\href{dimension_bound_prokhorov_20261015_proof_review.md}{frozen source
audit} records the exact primary provenance and the incomplete status of
the full 300 reconstruction.

Use Lorentz signature ((n,1)), outward facet normals of square 2, and
chamber inequalities ((h,\ensuremath{\alpha})\textless0). Acuteness
gives ((\ensuremath{\alpha},\ensuremath{\beta})\ensuremath{\le0}) for
different walls. Every nonzero negative pairing has magnitude at least
1: intersecting walls give
(2\texttt{\textbackslash{}cos}(\ensuremath{\pi}/m)),
(m\ensuremath{\ge3}), while parallel or disjoint walls give at least 2.
Thus no finite-label cutoff is needed.

At the assumed cusp there are (n) incident walls, with normals
(\ensuremath{\alpha}\emph{0,\texttt{\textbackslash{}ldots},\ensuremath{\alpha}}\{n-1\}).
Deleting node (i) gives a positive-definite rank-((n-1)) edge support
(S\_i). Its geometric edge has the original cusp as one endpoint. Choose
any additional facet (x\_i) at its other endpoint. Finite volume ensures
that endpoint is finite or ideal, not beyond the hyperbolic closure.
Consequently the Gram matrix on (S\_i\ensuremath{\cup}\{x\_i\}) is
positive semidefinite. This remains true at a nonsimple ideal endpoint;
no simplicity assumption is imposed there.

\section{1. Schur localization, without endpoint-diagram
enumeration}\label{schur-localization-without-endpoint-diagram-enumeration}

Write (J=G(S\_i)\^{}\{-1\}) and
(p\_j=-(x\_i,\ensuremath{\alpha}\_j)\ensuremath{\ge0}). Positive
semidefiniteness gives

\[
p_{S_i}^{T}Jp_{S_i}\le2.
\]

All entries of the inverses below are nonnegative. Thus
(J\_\{jj\}\textgreater2) forces (p\_j=0), because a nonzero Coxeter
contact has (p\_j\ensuremath{\ge1}).

The needed inverse formulas are elementary. For (A\_r), in path order
(a,b=0,\texttt{\textbackslash{}ldots},r-1),

\[
J_{ab}=\frac{(\min(a,b)+1)(r-\max(a,b))}{r+1}.
\]

For (B\_r), number the short end 0 and the remaining path
(1,\texttt{\textbackslash{}ldots},r-1), normalizing \textbf{all} roots
to square 2:

\[
J_{00}=r/2,\quad J_{0j}=(r-j)/\sqrt2,\quad
J_{ij}=r-\max(i,j)\quad(i,j\ge1).
\]

For (D\_r), use fork leaves 0,1, attached to 2, followed by the path to
(r-1):

\[
J_{00}=J_{11}=r/4,\quad J_{01}=(r-2)/4,
\quad J_{0j}=J_{1j}=(r-j)/2\ (j\ge2),
\quad J_{ij}=r-\max(i,j)\ (i,j\ge2).
\]

Multiplication by their sparse Gram matrices proves these identities for
every rank; all entries are positive. In (A\_\{n-1\}), every diagonal
except those within two positions of an end exceeds 2 when
(n\ensuremath{\ge10}). In (B\_r), the same assertion holds for
(r\ensuremath{\ge5}); in (D\_r), it holds for (r\ensuremath{\ge9}). The
two allowed end diagonals in (B,D) are 2 and 1.

It follows that, when the retained components meet those rank
thresholds, the full contact row of (x\_i) is supported only on

\[
\{i-2,i-1,i,i+1,i+2\}.
\]

For affine (A) the indices are cyclic. For the other families they are
interior path indices. The contact at the deleted node (i) itself is
unrestricted except by acuteness and the Coxeter gap; it has
\textbf{not} been assumed finite.

\section{2. A Lorentz row identity and its uniform lower
bound}\label{a-lorentz-row-identity-and-its-uniform-lower-bound}

Let (c=\ensuremath{\sum}\ensuremath{\delta}\_j\ensuremath{\alpha}\_j) be
a future null cusp vector, with positive affine coefficients. Put

\[
p_j=-(x,\alpha_j),\quad q_j=-(y,\alpha_j),\quad
\sigma=\sum\delta_jp_j=-(x,c),\quad
\tau=\sum\delta_jq_j=-(y,c).
\]

Both (\ensuremath{\sigma},\ensuremath{\tau}\textgreater0). A zero
contact row would make a norm-two vector orthogonal to the full cusp
span, whose orthogonal complement is the null line
(\texttt{\textbackslash{}mathbb\ }Rc), an impossibility. Let (E) be the
squared Euclidean norm of the image of
(x/\ensuremath{\sigma}-y/\ensuremath{\tau}) in
(c\^{}\texttt{\textbackslash{}perp}/\texttt{\textbackslash{}mathbb\ }Rc).
Directly expanding its square gives the exact identity

\[
\boxed{-(x,y)=\frac{\sigma\tau}{2}E-\frac{\sigma}{\tau}-\frac{\tau}{\sigma}.}
\]

If all possible contact positions have the same affine coefficient (d),
then the Coxeter gap gives
(\ensuremath{\sigma},\ensuremath{\tau}\ensuremath{\ge }d). When
(E\ensuremath{\ge4}/d\^{}2), the identity implies

\[
-(x,y)\ge\frac{d^2E}{2}-2.
\]

Indeed,
(1/\ensuremath{\sigma}\textsuperscript{2+1/\ensuremath{\tau}}2\ensuremath{\le2}/d\^{}2)
and (\ensuremath{\sigma}\ensuremath{\tau}\ensuremath{\ge }d\^{}2). This
removes any need for an upper bound on the unknown deleted-node
contacts, or a limiting argument involving those contacts.

\section{3. The path energy for affine
(B,C,D)}\label{the-path-energy-for-affine-bcd}

Write (m=n-1). In a null basis (c,d\_0) with ((c,d\_0)=-1), together
with orthonormal spatial coordinates
(e\_1,\texttt{\textbackslash{}ldots},e\_m), one may use:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  (\texttt{\textbackslash{}widetilde\ }C\_m):
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\_0=\ensuremath{\sqrt2}(c-e\_1)),
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\emph{j=e\_j-e}\{j+1\}) for
  (1\ensuremath{\le }j\textless m),
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\_m=\ensuremath{\sqrt2} e\_m). The affine
  coefficients are
  (1/\ensuremath{\sqrt2},1,\texttt{\textbackslash{}ldots},1,1/\ensuremath{\sqrt2}).
\item
  (\texttt{\textbackslash{}widetilde\ }B\_m):
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\_0=c-e\_1-e\_2),
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\_1=e\_1-e\_2),
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\emph{j=e\_j-e}\{j+1\}) for
  (2\ensuremath{\le }j\textless m),
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\_m=\ensuremath{\sqrt2} e\_m). The coefficients
  are (1,1,2,\texttt{\textbackslash{}ldots},2,\ensuremath{\sqrt2}).
\item
  (\texttt{\textbackslash{}widetilde\ }D\_m): the preceding first roots
  and interior chain, with final fork roots
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\emph{\{m-1\}=e}\{m-1\}-e\_m),
  (\ensuremath{\alpha}\emph{m=e}\{m-1\}+e\_m). The coefficients are
  (1,1,2,\texttt{\textbackslash{}ldots},2,1,1).
\end{itemize}

Deleting an interior node (i) leaves respectively

\[
B_i+B_{m-i},\qquad D_i+B_{m-i},\qquad D_i+D_{m-i}.
\]

After localization, all nonzero contacts are at interior nodes with
common coefficient (d=1,2,2), respectively. The spatial coordinates of a
normal with row (p) are, along the separating chain,

\[
z_k=-\sum_{\ell=k}^{m}p_\ell.
\]

For two rows supported within two nodes of (i\textless j), every
coordinate indexed from (i+3) through (j-2) has normalized difference
exactly (1/d) in absolute value. One row has no remaining mass there and
the other has total contact mass (\ensuremath{\tau}/d). Therefore

\[
E\ge\frac{j-i-4}{d^2},\qquad
-(x_i,x_j)\ge\frac{j-i-4}{2}-2
\quad\text{if }j-i-4\ge4.
\]

Let (s) be the node of the narrow facet. Initially choose the deleted
nodes as follows:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Family & Initial (i,j) & Component rank requirements \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
(C\_m) & (5,m-5) & both (B) ranks at least 5 \\
(B\_m) & (9,m-5) & (D) rank at least 9, (B) rank at least 5 \\
(D\_m) & (9,m-9) & both (D) ranks at least 9 \\
\end{longtable}
}

If (s=i), increase (i) by one; if (s=j), decrease (j) by one. At the
excluded ranks these alternatives are disjoint, so at most one move
occurs. All retained-component thresholds remain true. The resulting
negative pairings are at least

\[
\frac{m-19}{2},\qquad \frac{m-23}{2},\qquad \frac{m-27}{2},
\]

respectively. They reach 14 at (m=47,51,55).

\section{4. The cycle energy for affine
(A)}\label{the-cycle-energy-for-affine-a}

The affine (A\_\{n-1\}) Gram matrix is the cycle Laplacian; all null
coefficients equal 1. The normalized row difference has total charge
zero, with positive mass 1 in the five-node interval about (i) and
negative mass 1 in the interval about (j).

The Euclidean energy (E) is the electrical flow energy on this cycle.
This follows either by solving the root-coordinate differences or from
the Laplacian pseudoinverse. On the two long arcs separating the contact
intervals, conservation makes the flow constant, with respective values
(u) and (u-1). If their lengths are (L\_1,L\_2), all remaining edge
energies are nonnegative, and

\[
E\ge L_1u^2+L_2(u-1)^2
\ge \frac{L_1L_2}{L_1+L_2}.
\]

The last inequality is the identity obtained by subtracting the right
side and leaving (((L\_1+L\_2)u-L\_2)\^{}2/(L\_1+L\_2)). It covers
arbitrary nonnegative contact distributions, not just single-node rows.

Choose opposite deleted nodes, avoiding (s) by rotating both one step if
needed. Then

\[
L_1=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-4,\qquad L_2=\lceil n/2\rceil-4.
\]

For (n\ensuremath{\ge136}), both lengths are at least 64, so
(E\ensuremath{\ge32}) and (-(x\_i,x\_j)\ensuremath{\ge14}). This
recovers the linear separation mechanism of Nikulin's worked affine-(A)
example with an explicit boundary.

\section{5. Why these are genuinely framing walls of the narrow
facet}\label{why-these-are-genuinely-framing-walls-of-the-narrow-facet}

This incidence bridge is essential. Avoiding (s) means that the
narrow-facet root belongs to both retained edge supports. Its inverse
diagonal is at least 1 in the path cases, and at least
((n-1)/n\textgreater1/2) in the cycle case. The Schur bound therefore
gives

\[
|(x_i,\alpha_s)|<2.
\]

Thus their rank-two Gram is positive definite; the two hyperplanes meet
\textbf{inside} hyperbolic space. More strongly, they share an actual
ridge of (P). To see this, project a strict interior point (h) onto
their common orthogonal complement. The inverse Gram is entrywise
nonnegative, while the two pairings with (h) are negative. Consequently
the projection has negative square and its pairing with every other wall
remains strictly negative by acuteness. It is a point of the relative
interior of that ridge. This argument does not rely on the terminating
edge endpoint being finite.

Both terminating walls therefore belong to exactly the set controlled by
the narrow-facet theorem. If their pairing is at most (-14), their
hyperplane distance is at least (\ensuremath{\operatorname{arccosh}}7),
contradicting the published strict upper bound. The four dimension
bounds follow.

\section{Scope and the remaining
problem}\label{scope-and-the-remaining-problem}

This proof closes the full-rank irreducible classical cusp calculation.
The exceptional irreducible affine types have bounded rank at most 9;
thus, using the standard affine classification, any \textbf{irreducible}
cusp on the chosen narrow facet has ambient dimension at most 135. This
is a conditional statement about that particular narrow facet. A
noncompact polytope may have a narrow facet with only finite vertices,
and a nonsimple ideal vertex has a product cusp diagram. Neither case is
eliminated here.

For context,
\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0502413}{Felikson--Tumarkin's primary
theorem} already gives (n\ensuremath{\le8}) when the entire polytope is
both simple and ideal. Their ideal hypothesis means every vertex is
ideal, and is substantially stronger than the local hypothesis used
here. The present bounds are proof-reconstruction lemmas, not a claim to
improve that theorem or a verified new global bound for simple
finite-volume polytopes.

For a product cusp the affine null vectors of the different factors are
proportional but have independent relative scales. The row identity
survives after choosing one common null vector. The localization and
energy arguments above cannot simply be summed: an outgoing edge omits a
node in \textbf{each} affine factor, and a terminating wall may
distribute its contacts across those factors. Controlling that
distribution and the narrow-facet incidence uniformly is the next
unresolved problem. No claim that terminating walls contact only one
component is used or justified here.
